titulo: Intelligent Failure Prediction in CI/CD Pipelines Using Efficient Machine Learning Techniques
titulo_norm: intelligent failure prediction in ci cd pipelines using efficient machine learning techniques
resumo: In modern software development, where large systems are being replaced by smaller, microservices-based ones, a major challenge is building a single defect prediction model that works across different programming languages, especially within the fast-paced environment of CI/CD pipelines. This study proposes a reinforcement learning-based approach by formulating the CI/CD pipeline optimization as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling intelligent failure prediction and decision-making. Experimental evaluations were conducted using a high-performance Google Colab environment. The proposed MDP model achieved a high classification accuracy of 93.7%, with a precision of 90.65%, recall of 95.25%, and an F1-score of 90.5%, outperforming conventional models like SVM and AdaBoost. Resource utilization analysis revealed efficient performance with 81% CPU usage, 709 MB memory usage, and a low-test redundancy rate of 17%. The confusion matrix and reward-driven design demonstrate the model's robustness in identifying failures accurately while minimizing redundant operations. These findings validate the MDP model as an effective and efficient solution for predictive maintenance in CI/CD systems.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Structural condition assessment and prediction using machine learning-based EKF
titulo_norm: structural condition assessment and prediction using machine learning based ekf
resumo: This paper aims to improve the machine learning (ML)-based extended-Kalman filter (EKF) technique for condition assessment of structures. EKF is widely used for estimating structural properties, aiding in the detection and assessment of damage. However, it lacks accuracy in the prediction of aging and remaining service life. This study improves the prediction of structural conditions by incorporating ML algorithms, thus facilitating timely predictive maintenance and disaster prevention strategies. The proposed method employs EKF for the parameter estimation from vibration responses to train ML models for accurate prediction. The framework is validated based on multi-storey framed structures subjected to seismic excitation through numerical simulations and experimental tests. The results illustrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method up to 20% Gaussian and non-Gaussian noises. The ML model such as extreme gradient boosting achieves R2 score of 0.99 and RMSE of approx. 0.01 in predicting the stiffness parameters. The proposed approach demonstrates potential in real-time condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Copyright © 2025 Inderscience Enterprises Ltd.

titulo: PREDICTIVE REPAIR MANAGEMENT USING MULTI-HEAD ATTENTION TRANSFORMER AND ONLINE LEARNING
titulo_norm: predictive repair management using multi head attention transformer and online learning
resumo: Accurate prediction of repair durations is a challenge in product maintenance due to its implications for resource allocation, customer satisfaction, and operational performance. This study aims to develop a deep learning framework to help fleet repair shops accurately categorize repair time given product historical data. The study uses an automobile repair and maintenance dataset and creates an end-to-end predictive framework by employing a multi-head attention network designed for tabular data. The developed framework combines categorical information, transformed through embeddings and attention mechanisms, with numerical historical data to facilitate integration and learning from diverse data features. A weighted loss function is introduced to overcome class imbalance issues in large datasets. Moreover, an online learning strategy is used for continuous incremental model updates to maintain predictive accuracy in evolving operational environments. Our empirical findings demonstrate that the multi-head attention mechanism extracts meaningful interactions between vehicle identifiers and repair types compared to a feed-forward neural network. Also, combining historical maintenance data with an online learning strategy facilitates real-time adjustments to changing patterns and increases the model’s predictive performance on new data. The model is tested on real-world repair data spanning 2013 to 2020 and achieves an accuracy of 78%, with attention weight analyses illustrating feature interactions. © 2025 by ASME.

titulo: Digital twins, artificial intelligence and immersive technologies for heritage preservation and cultural tourism in smart cities
titulo_norm: digital twins artificial intelligence and immersive technologies for heritage preservation and cultural tourism in smart cities
resumo: The idea of the digital twin (DT) originated in NASA’s Apollo Space Program during the 1970s, but it was formally defined by Michael Grieves in 2002 as the “virtual representation of what has been produced.” Initially, from 1970 to 2000, DTs were mainly applied in astronautics and aerospace. However, since 2001, their use has expanded into the industrial sector, with significant applications in the manufacturing, aerospace, and automotive industries. This cultural shift improved their application in creating, constructing, and overseeing virtual products grounded in real-world parameters, with an increased focus on informatics (since 2011), construction (since 2016), and heritage (since 2020) sectors. In these contexts, DTs replicate the physical behavior of heritage objects within virtual environments, facilitating multiphysics modeling and continuous model updates through automated data monitoring. In the realm of heritage and tourism in smart cities, DTs have found diverse applications, spanning pathology mapping, predictive maintenance, energy simulation, building management, and virtual and augmented reality. Their integration is intricately linked with concepts such as the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in devising devices for monitoring microclimatic conditions, airflow, air quality, noise, and lighting pollution to assist in the proactive preservation of artifacts, predicting deterioration patterns, and recommending optimal conservation measures. Also, Heritage Building Information Modeling can help with concept design, construction, scheduling, estimation, and prediction. Immersive technologies and AI-driven DTs can enhance visitor experiences through personalized interactive guides, immersive storytelling, and virtual reconstructions of historical sites. Integrating blockchain technology can secure provenance data, ensuring the authenticity of heritage items. This chapter will delve into the evolution and applications of DT, AI, and immersive technologies in the heritage and tourist sectors, with a focus on the integration with blockchain to promise innovative and sustainable approaches for engaging and safeguarding the cultural legacy. This concept gives rise to the “Heritage 4.0” framework, where industrial production, cyber-physical systems, and digital and computational technologies come together. © 2025 Elsevier Inc. titulo: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Downtime Optimization in Water Treatment Plants
titulo_norm: ai driven predictive maintenance and downtime optimization in water treatment plants
resumo: This chapter presents a comprehensive analysis of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive maintenance (PdM) systems and their implementation in water treatment facilities. The study examines the evolution from traditional reactive maintenance to sophisticated predictive approaches, emphasizing the integration of AI, machine learning, and digital twin technologies. Through a systematic review of recent implementations and technological advances, we investigate how these systems optimize operational efficiency and reduce downtime in water treatment operations. The methodology encompasses data collection frameworks, AI model development architectures, and performance evaluation metrics, supported by real-world case studies from multiple facilities. Results demonstrate significant improvements in fault detection accuracy (up to 99.50% with stacked convolutional autoencoder models) and substantial reductions in operational costs (25% in the first year) and high-level alarms (97% reduction). The challenges identified include data integration complexities, initial investment requirements, and workforce training needs. The research highlights the transformative potential of AI-driven PdM while acknowledging implementation barriers and future development opportunities. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Smriti Agarwal and Manoj Chandra Garg; individual chapters, the contributors. titulo: Analysis of Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings Using AI
titulo_norm: analysis of energy efficiency in public buildings using ai
resumo: The management of energy efficiency in public buildings has emerged as a prominent target as urban areas aim to diminish their environmental impact and increase their sustainability. This study focuses on the utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) in the analysis and improvement of energy efficiency in public buildings. AI models are developed by processing data from diverse energy-consuming systems such as lighting, the HVAC system (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) as well as occupancy sensors; these models subsequently identify patterns and inefficiencies that crimp excessive energy. The research recommends a conceptual framework for continuous monitoring and adaptive control, using machine learning algorithms to optimize energy consumption by dynamically. This AI-based approach aspires for maximum energy savings in combination with sufficient indoor comfort and is a long-term strategy regarding energy sustainability for public institutions scaling it. Drives for change are showing that the research of past energy efficiency programs, in addition to actual energy measurements, can be plugged into predicting energy needs in the future. The outcomes suggest that the application of AI in energy management can be the factor that decisively lowers electricity payments, reduces the carbon footprint through the use of renewable energy, and forms public amenities that are green and intelligent.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Powered Fault Detection Predictive Maintenance for Industrial Machinery a Reliability Engineering Perspective
titulo_norm: artificial intelligence ai powered fault detection predictive maintenance for industrial machinery a reliability engineering perspective
resumo: With the increasing complexity of industrial machinery under the industry 4.0 paradigm, advanced and intelligent fault detection techniques are essential to ensure operational efficiency and reduce unplanned downtime. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on manual feature engineering and struggle to adapt to dynamic operational environments, prompting the shift toward deep learning-based solutions. This study presents a robust AI-driven fault detection framework using a 1D-Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN), trained on the Paderborn University (PU) dataset, for predictive maintenance applications. The model processes raw time-series data from multiple sensors, enhanced through overlapping window segmentation, and is evaluated using standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score. The 1D-CNN demonstrates outstanding classification capability, outperforming conventional classifiers such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), Regularized Fisher Discriminant Analysis (RFDA), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Its high training and testing accuracy, along with strong generalization, validates the model's suitability for real-world industrial deployment. This research highlights the significance of deep learning in building more reliable, scalable, and automated predictive maintenance systems, contributing to increased equipment uptime and operational safety.  © 2025 IEEE.

Digital twinning of battery packs is one example of a state-of-the-art method. To enhance the performance, security, and efficient, digital twins (DTs) of batteries use progressed multidimensional models, AI, sophisticated sensor element, IoT technologies, and cloud computing strategies toward create a fundamental, active illustration about actual battery system (physical twin). An exhaustive examination of the necessary supporting technologies, demands, & several possible applications for battery DTs is presented in this review paper. Included in the scope of the review are software architectures, use cases, digital platforms that facilitate DT creation and integration, software, and hardware requirements for DT implementation with batteries, electrical considerations for modeling, and algorithmic methodologies. The present challenges are identified, and scenarios that will yield enough benefit to compensate for these challenges, such as the extra costs, are discussed. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Ontology-driven LLM framework for knowledge graph in smart buildings
titulo_norm: ontology driven llm framework for knowledge graph in smart buildings
resumo: The rapid data growth in smart building environments requires advanced tools to integrate, interpret, and utilize this information effectively. Smart buildings generate vast and heterogeneous data streams, including sensor readings, occupancy metrics, and environmental conditions, which are critical for optimizing energy efficiency, enhancing occupant comfort, and enabling predictive maintenance. However, the lack of a structured approach to automatically connect and contextualize these data sources limits the insights that can be derived. To address these challenges, this paper presents a framework for assessing data in a knowledge graph by automatically retrieving entities and establishing relationships from diverse data sources, incorporating metadata standards and time-series data relevant to smart buildings. A standard ontology from the domain is used to drive the experiment, enabling the automatic construction of a semantic graph-based model for a real-world smart building environment. The framework’s objective is to ensure information is comprehensible as a preliminary step to intelligent decision-making in data-driven smart buildings, enabling applications like fault detection, performance measurement, and energy auditing. The proposed approach explores the potential of large language models (LLMs) to automate data integration, reducing reliance on experts. This paper addresses existing literature gaps on metadata mapping and lays the groundwork for future advancements in digital twin technologies for smart building applications. © 2025 Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction. titulo: Edge AI-Driven Vision Systems for Zero-Defect Manufacturing in 6G-Enabled Industry 5.0: The Factory of the Future
titulo_norm: edge ai driven vision systems for zero defect manufacturing in 6g enabled industry 5 0 the factory of the future
resumo: In the era of Industry 5.0, achieving zero-defect manufacturing is essential for enhancing production quality, minimizing waste, and ensuring operational efficiency. Traditional quality control systems - whether manual or cloud-based - face challenges such as high latency, limited scalability, and data security risks. This paper presents a novel Edge AIdriven vision system that leverages 6G connectivity to enable real-time defect detection on the manufacturing floor. The proposed solution integrates lightweight deep learning models and high-speed edge inference to eliminate the need for centralized processing, thereby reducing response times and energy consumption. Experimental validation using NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier demonstrates significant performance gains, including 99.2% defect detection accuracy, a 70% reduction in latency, and 40% lower energy consumption compared to conventional cloud-based approaches. These results underscore the system's potential to facilitate predictive maintenance, seamless human-AI collaboration, and real-time defect elimination - core principles of Industry 5.0. Despite these advancements, challenges such as model optimization for edge hardware, secure federated learning, and widespread 6G infrastructure adoption remain open research problems. Future work will focus on integrating neuromorphic computing and blockchain-enhanced AI for improved adaptability, security, and scalability. This research lays a strong foundation for intelligent, autonomous, and defect-free manufacturing in nextgeneration smart factories. © 2025 IEEE.

The system amalgamates diverse sensors with IoT connections, facilitating real-time data acquisition and processing. Machine learning algorithms, such as linear regression, multiple regression, and k-nearest neighbors (KNN), were utilized to forecast system efficiency and identify potential hazards. The system reliably predicts hazardous conditions, with linear regression demonstrating the highest accuracy in gas burner stability. Its cost-effective design makes it suitable for industrial use The system's efficiency, particularly in delivering early alerts and enabling proactive measures, provides a sense of security. Future efforts will optimize the system to improve resilience in dynamic industrial settings. The proposed approach enhances safety protocols in the chemical industry. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance Models for Structural Health Monitoring in Civil Engineering Using Deep Learning and IoT Sensors

resumo: By enabling predictive maintenance systems that can contribute to the safety of infrastructure development, dependability and longevity of structures, the combination of artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors are making waves in structural health monitoring (SHM) in civil engineering. There are various SHM methods in use that are frequently based on reactive maintenance and/or a cycle-based method of inspection which may be expensive and inefficient. AI-driven predictive maintenance, on the other hand, takes real-time data from IoT-enabled sensors installed in a civil structure and uses the data to monitor variables, such as displacement, temperature, stress and vibration. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are two types of DL algorithms that are used to analyse complex data from sensors to help identify trends, as well as potential structural problems before they happen. Proactive method of maintenance and detection of anomalies in the past are made easier thanks to the continuous learning and accuracy of such models. This way, as there is an improvement in terms of public safety, reduction in maintenance costs, least downtime. The integration of DL and IoT in SHM is delivering a datadriven and scalable architecture that allows bridges, buildings, dams and other important infrastructures to be managed intelligently. To illustrate the revolutionary implication of intelligent SHM in the contemporary civil engineering application, this paper will discuss the architecture of the AI-based predictive maintenance system, elaborate on the issues of implementation and the latest development. © 2025 IEEE.

resumo: This research presents an ontology-driven framework for integrating building information modeling (BIM) and facility management (FM) systems with Internet of Things (IoT) data streams to address key interoperability barriers - conceptual, semantic, organizational, and technological. Traditional approaches are limited by fragmented workflows, static data standards, and manual processes, which limit their scalability and adaptability. Leveraging Neo4j for semantic modeling, Python for automated data integration and anomaly detection, and Power Automate for real-time workflow execution, the proposed framework ensures seamless interoperability, scalability, and dynamic task automation. A simulated HVAC maintenance scenario validates its effectiveness, demonstrating 75%-90% reductions in task execution times, 81% overall time savings, and 98% semantic model accuracy. These results highlight the framework's ability to resolve interoperability challenges, automate workflows, and advance intelligent, data-driven facility management practices. © ASCE.

titulo: From Code to Sustainability: The Impact of Computer Science in Advancing Sustainable Development
titulo_norm: from code to sustainability the impact of computer science in advancing sustainable development
resumo: In an era defined by unprecedented challenges to global sustainability, the dynamic interplay between artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) has emerged as a transformative force in fostering innovative solutions for pressing environmental, social, and economic issues. This chapter delves into the pivotal role that AI and ML technologies play in advancing the cause of sustainable development across diverse sectors and domains. In this comprehensive chapter, we explore the integral role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in propelling sustainable development across critical sectors. Embracing the imperatives of our time, this chapter provides a holistic overview of how AI and ML synergistically empower advancements in energy efficiency, renewable energy integration, environmental monitoring, precision agriculture, smart transportation, waste management, and sustainable urban planning. This chapter initiates by contextualizing the pervasive influence of AI and ML in revolutionizing conventional paradigms. It emphasizes their potential to transcend disciplinary boundaries and generate innovative solutions to multifaceted challenges. Each of the covered fields is meticulously examined, illuminating how AI-driven predictive modeling, data analytics, and real-time decision-making contribute to fostering a more sustainable future. In energy efficiency, AI-enabled insights optimize energy consumption patterns, reduce waste, and enhance operational efficiency. Renewable energy integration harnesses ML algorithms to seamlessly integrate diverse renewable sources into the power grid, propelling the transition toward cleaner energy systems. Environmental monitoring witnesses the transformational power of AI-driven remote sensing and data analytics in tracking ecological shifts, managing natural resources, and mitigating environmental risks. In precision agriculture, AI and ML redefine farming practices through data-driven insights that optimize resource allocation, increase crop yields, and minimize environmental impacts. The Smart Transportation landscape benefits from AI-enhanced traffic management, predictive maintenance, and autonomous vehicles, leading to reduced congestion and emissions. Waste Management embraces AI-optimized collection routes and recycling practices, contributing to waste reduction and sustainable resource management. Lastly, this chapter delves into how AI and ML converge to forge the future of Sustainable Urban Planning. The technologies facilitate informed decision-making in urban design, infrastructure management, and citizen engagement, fostering resilient and inclusive cities. As AI and ML revolutionize these domains, this chapter underscores the ethical considerations paramount to responsible deployment. It contemplates challenges concerning data privacy, algorithmic bias, and social equity, emphasizing the significance of ensuring ethical and equitable outcomes. This comprehensive chapter envisions a future shaped by AI and ML’s transformative potential, cultivating cross-disciplinary collaborations and catalyzing global efforts toward sustainable development. As AI and ML continue to redefine the boundaries of innovation, this chapter serves as a roadmap for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers navigating the dynamic landscape of sustainable development. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2024.

titulo: IoT-Driven Transformer Health Monitoring using LSTM Models in High-Voltage Substations
titulo_norm: iot driven transformer health monitoring using lstm models in high voltage substations
resumo: The maintenance and dependability of high-voltage substations are essential for maintaining the stability of power distribution networks. This research introduces an IoT-based methodology for monitoring transformer health using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. Through the integration of IoT sensors, real-time data about transformer characteristics, including temperature, pressure, and vibration, is perpetually gathered and sent to a centralized monitoring system. The LSTM model, recognized for its efficacy in time-series data forecasting, is used to examine historical and real-time data, facilitating anomaly identification and the prediction of probable failures. The research illustrates the use of this technology in improving predictive maintenance plans for transformers, hence minimizing downtime and operating expenses. Experimental findings demonstrate that the LSTM model significantly enhances the precision of health evaluations relative to conventional monitoring techniques. This unique approach enhances proactive maintenance procedures and improves the efficiency and durability of high-voltage substations, providing a stable power supply. The proposed method may be expanded and used in other essential infrastructure elements within the energy industry, facilitating the development of more intelligent and robust power grids.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Towards intelligent HVAC systems: Leveraging AI for sustainable energy management
titulo_norm: towards intelligent hvac systems leveraging ai for sustainable energy management
resumo: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into the predictive management of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems optimizes energy efficiency, reducing costs, and improving occupant comfort. HVAC systems are essential for healthy indoor environments. These systems can consume up to 40% of a building's energy. Inefficient management leads to energy waste and premature equipment wear. The present study provides an analysis of historical and real-time data. predictive management forecasts temperature variations, energy demand peak, potential equipment failures, and maintenance needs. Thanks to AI, in particular machine learning, neural networks, IoT, Big Data and Edge Computing, energy consumption optimization anticipates breakdowns and improves comfort by reducing the carbon footprint. Based on a case study, significant improvements in several key areas were demonstrated after implementing the AI-powered predictive management system. Secondly, Predictive optimization led to an average reduction in energy consumption of 25%. Hence, integrating AI into the predictive management of HVAC systems offers opportunities to improve energy efficiency, reduce costs and contribute to a sustainable future. titulo: Transformer neural networks in Industry 4.0
titulo_norm: transformer neural networks in industry 4 0
resumo: This paper investigates the emerging role of transformer-based neural networks in advancing Industry 4.0, where the rapid generation of unstructured data—from maintenance logs to sensor readings —necessitates robust analytical tools. We begin by examining the core architecture of transformers, highlighting self-attention and parallel processing as key innovations that facilitate long-range dependency modeling. We then explore how these capabilities address critical Industry 4.0 needs, such as predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, and defect localization. Case studies in text-based log analysis demonstrate significant accuracy gains—often exceeding 90%—when compared to conventional methods like regex-based parsing or RNNs. Similarly, Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel in quality control tasks, accurately identifying subtle defects under challenging conditions. In the realm of time-series sensor data, transformer architectures capture intricate temporal correlations, enabling early fault detection and forecasting of remaining useful life. Despite these successes, the paper also notes practical challenges, including computational demands, the need for interpretability, and deployment constraints on industrial edge devices. Concluding remarks emphasize that transformer-based AI stands as a cornerstone for Industry 4.0, offering a flexible and powerful framework to tackle the complexity of modern manufacturing environments while suggesting avenues for future research in optimization and domain-specific customization. © 2025 Copyright for this paper by its authors. titulo: Defect Detection in Aircraft Materials using Generative AI and Deep Learning - A Review
titulo_norm: defect detection in aircraft materials using generative ai and deep learning a review
resumo: Aircraft maintenance plays a crucial role in ensuring safety, reliability, and cost-effectiveness in aviation. Traditional defect detection methods, such as manual inspections, are labor-intensive and prone to human error. Advances in deep learning and computer vision have led to automated detection systems, significantly enhancing efficiency and accuracy. Recent studies have demonstrated the application of deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures, in detecting defects in aircraft engine borescopes, fuselage surfaces, and aero-engine blades. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with AI-driven inspection systems further improve defect detection in aircraft skin and light aircraft components. Hybrid transformer architectures and generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown promise in surface defect detection, enabling precise identification and classification of structural abnormalities. Additionally, predictive maintenance strategies integrating generative AI and deep learning facilitate proactive identification of potential failures, reducing aircraft downtime and maintenance costs. Data augmentation techniques, including synthetic defect generation and semi-supervised learning, enhance model generalization, particularly for imbalanced datasets. This study consolidates existing research on AI-based defect detection in aircraft maintenance, emphasizing the transformative potential of machine learning for automated inspections, predictive maintenance, aircraft health monitoring, and future research in the domain. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance Using AI in the Mechatronics Industry
titulo_norm: fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance using ai in the mechatronics industry
resumo: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance (PdM) or smart maintenance in the mechatronics industry (MI). As complex mechatronic systems become more prevalent in numerous sectors, the necessity for efficient and practical maintenance strategies has grown significantly. This chapter explores merging advanced AI approaches, bringing in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), to improve accuracy of fault diagnosis and facilitate PdM in mechatronics. The first part of the chapter investigates the advancements in AI algorithms (models) that expedite fault diagnosis by analyzing data from sensors, system behavior, and historical patterns. AI-powered fault diagnosis promptly detects anomalies and identifies underlying root sources, reducing downtime and increasing system productivity and reliability. Further, the chapter focuses on the use of PdM techniques that should be put into practice depending on AI prognostics. As it relates to maintenance task management, the assessment of its remaining useful life (RUL) makes it possible to schedule tasks effectively and optimally deploy both human and machine resources, to secure the usage of expensive equipment for a longer time and optimize the use of spare parts. Actual applications of mechatronics are described to prove the potential gains for fault diagnosis and PdM powered by AI. Finally, the difficulties and trends of AI in the MI domain are described which indicate the direction for future study and development of this innovative discipline. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Pushpalatha Naveenkumar, Vandana Sharma, Gunapriya Devarajan, Azween Abdullah, and Ahmed A. titulo: AI-powered urban infrastructure monitoring using RADAR-based remote sensing
titulo_norm: ai powered urban infrastructure monitoring using radar based remote sensing
resumo: This chapter explores how artificial intelligence (AI) drives a paradigm shift in RADAR-based remote sensing for urban infrastructure monitoring. Urban monitoring has shifted toward a predictive and proactive approach by harnessing RADAR’s ability to penetrate materials and AI’s advanced data processing techniques. This chapter examines how AI can be applied to RADAR data for tracking changes in infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and underground facilities, and identifying risks related to ground subsidence. The discussion includes AI-driven methodologies for structural assessment, urban expansion analysis, and predictive infrastructure maintenance. titulo: A Novel Method for Experimental Fault Simulation and Remaining Useful Life Estimation in Bearings
titulo_norm: a novel method for experimental fault simulation and remaining useful life estimation in bearings
resumo: Predictive maintenance, through regular monitoring of the actual electromechanical condition, efficiency, and other operational indicators of machines and process systems, ensures maximum intervals between repairs and reduces the frequency and cost of unplanned shutdowns caused by failures. Therefore, it is essential to develop efficient methodologies that are feasible for implementation in industrial plants, enabling control and predictability of maintenance downtime. In this context, the Envelope Technique - a reference method for fault analysis, diagnosis, and monitoring in bearings - is applied through frequency-domain spectral analysis of vibration signals, based on the propagation of amplitude near the natural frequency of the component under analysis. This work presents a simple, efficient, and innovative methodology for experimental simulations, monitoring, diagnosis, fault prediction, and estimation of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of bearings in rotating machines using vibration signals acquired by a sensor installed on a test bench specifically designed and built to replicate the dynamics of real-world rotating machinery. The implemented experimental simulations generated the progressive increase of vibration peaks - characteristic of fault evolution - through a novel method involving the controlled application of dynamic radial loads. Vibration spectral datasets were collected from an MPU6050 sensor via an Arduino Mega 2560 board, integrated with a model developed in Simulink, which enabled real-time signal acquisition and data file generation for critical (or admissible) fault prediction through processing in MATLAB. The prediction of the critical fault occurrence and RUL estimation was performed using a simple numerical method based on successive function approximation, which allowed the derivation of a characteristic degradation function for the system. Measurements were conducted on both healthy and defect-induced ball bearings under different applied radial loads. The methodology proved efficient and easy to implement in real-world industrial applications, yielding RUL estimates with errors below 25 %, and in some cases, as low as 5 %. The most accurate RUL predictions were obtained when the signal acquisition rate exceeded 15 times the natural frequency (fn) of the component under study. The procedures developed in this work can be effectively applied in industrial environments to predict the occurrence of critical bearing failures in advance and may be adapted for monitoring other components and systems, including nuclear facilities, enabling accurate and reliable RUL estimation.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Enhancing System-Level Prognostics with Structural Information: A Graph-Based Approach
titulo_norm: enhancing system level prognostics with structural information a graph based approach
resumo: Effective system-level prognostics is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of complex industrial systems, such as nuclear power plants. This study proposes a novel framework for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of a system by integrating component-level degradation, system topology, and machine learning. A system health index is derived using stress and health functions, normalized across components, and aggregated based on the system's topology. Four machine learning models - Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR), Fully Connected Neural Network (FCNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and Graph Neural Network (GNN) - are evaluated using simulation data from the Asherah Nuclear Power Plant Simulator (ANS). The results demonstrate that the GNN outperforms other models in both accuracy and consistency, highlighting the advantage of capturing system structure in prognostic tasks. Visual and numerical metrics confirm the GNN's ability to provide reliable RUL predictions with a compact architecture. This study underscores the potential of graph-based learning for system-level prognostics and lays the foundation for further advancements in system-level predictive maintenance strategies for critical infrastructure. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: A Lightweight Device Management Platform Integrating Multi-source Data Modeling and Intelligent Scheduling
titulo_norm: a lightweight device management platform integrating multi source data modeling and intelligent scheduling
resumo: In storage and transportation systems, electrical and mechanical equipment such as conveyors, pumps, valves, and loading arms operate under prolonged high-load, corrosive, and frequent start-stop conditions. Traditional Time-Based Maintenance (TBM) and empirical risk assessment methods struggle to fully utilize historical failures and multi-source data, making it challenging to support department-level precision maintenance and workforce allocation. This paper addresses scenarios in storage and transportation departments by constructing a multi-source data model centered on a five-level BOM/EBS structure. The model integrates a six-dimensional degradation risk matrix, historical failure records, and maintenance plans, employing gradient boosting trees to predict future equipment failure probabilities. These predictions are combined with expert ratings to generate comprehensive risk levels. Building on this foundation, the maintenance cycle and position workload optimization are modeled as a resource-constrained 0-1 integer programming problem. By balancing risk exposure, downtime duration, and labor costs as multi-objective criteria, the system generates equipment-level maintenance cycle and position workload allocation plans. The platform adopts a front-end and backend separated Web architecture to visually display multisource data, risk predictions, and optimization results. Realworld data from a storage and transportation department demonstrates that compared to fixed-cycle TBM schemes, the proposed AI-driven strategy significantly improves high-risk equipment identification rates, focuses maintenance efforts on critical equipment, reduces failure rates and downtime duration, and provides quantitative evidence for workforce allocation. learning; integer programming; equipment management platform; storage and transportation system © 2025 IEEE.

Fault scenarios, including ground faults, short circuits, and panel degradation, are simulated, with sensor data collected in real time using strategically deployed voltage, current, temperature, irradiance, and vibration sensors. The data is processed into a comprehensive dataset for machine learning analysis. Algorithms such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Neural Networks are evaluated, with model performance validated using metrics like accuracy, precision, and F1score. IoT integration facilitates real-time alerts to mobile devices, ensuring timely fault responses. The proposed framework achieves high fault classification accuracy and enhances operational safety by minimizing downtime. Its scalability makes it adaptable to various solar plant configurations, offering a robust solution for renewable energy management. This study underscores the potential of combining IoT and machine learning to optimize solar plant reliability and efficiency while enabling advancements in predictive maintenance. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo_norm: combining expert knowledge and deep learning with case based reasoning for predictive maintenance
resumo: If a manufacturing company's main goal is to sell products profitably, protecting production systems from defects is essential and has led to vast documentation and expert knowledge. Industry 4.0 has facilitated access to sensor and operational data across the shop floor, enabling data-driven models that detect faults and predict failures, which are crucial for predictive maintenance to minimize unplanned downtimes and costs. Commonly, a universally applicable machine learning (ML) approach is used without explicitly integrating prior knowledge from sources beyond training data, risking incorrect rediscovery or neglecting already existing knowledge. Integrating expert knowledge with ML can address the scarcity of failure examples and avoid the learning of spurious correlations, though it poses technical challenges when combining Semantic Web-based knowledge graphs with neural networks (NNs) for time series data. The three most common machine learning algorithms, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest, were compared in comprehensive detail with all types of sensor data: electricity, chilled water, hot water, and steam. Unlike previous research, which has usually focused on a single model or limited evaluation criteria, the research compared multiple models on seven different performance metrics such as RMSE, R2 MAE, SMAPE, MSLE, F1 Score, and Precision. resumo: This paper introduces BIM-Fence, a dynamic indoor zoning risk management system that integrates BIM, computer vision, and digital twin technologies. The system aims to enhance building operation and maintenance by providing real-time risk alerts based on user location within a space. BIM-Fence employs a three-step process: 1. The system was tested in a campus digital fabrication workshop, demonstrating its ability to identify high-risk zones and issue dynamic alerts. By leveraging BIM as a management interface, this research advances the use of BIM-based digital twins system for dynamic crowd risk management, contributing to building operation management. © 2025 and published by the Association for Computer-Aided Architectural Design Research in Asia (CAADRIA), Hong Kong.

resumo: Current building inspections are mainly relied on human, making the process time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, the development of deep-learning-based automated inspection systems has become a growing trend. However, the lack of a comprehensive training dataset is the majority challenge in developing deep-learning models. To bridge this gap, we introduce CUBIT-CW, a human-annotated dataset containing 10871 high-resolution images collected via drone, with multiscale ranging from 800 × 600 to 8000 × 6000 pixels. It also works for instance segmentation, allowing for the models to have a detailed understanding of defect boundaries and features. To evaluate its effectiveness, we test CUBIT-CW by 6 state-of-the-art(SOTA) computer vision models. titulo: Smart Infrastructure Management: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Precision Crack Detection and Maintenance
titulo_norm: smart infrastructure management leveraging artificial intelligence for precision crack detection and maintenance
resumo: The effective management and maintenance of civil infrastructure, particularly in buildings, are vital for ensuring structural integrity and safety. This paper investigates the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing precision crack detection and maintenance of building infrastructure. Traditional methods of crack detection often rely on manual inspections, which can be time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to human error. AI technologies, particularly machine learning and computer vision, offer significant advancements in automating and improving the accuracy of crack detection. By employing AI-driven systems, real-time data from various sensors and imaging devices can be analyzed to identify and classify cracks with high precision. These systems can detect minute cracks that might be overlooked by human inspectors, thus preventing minor issues from escalating into major structural problems. The integration of AI with other modern tools such as drones and robotic inspection devices further enhances the reach and effectiveness of monitoring efforts. Moreover, AI can assist in predictive maintenance by analyzing patterns and trends from historical and real-time data, enabling proactive maintenance strategies. This approach not only enhances the safety and durability of buildings but also reduces maintenance costs and downtime. The paper also discusses the challenges of implementing AI in crack detection, including the need for large datasets for training algorithms, the complexity of integrating AI with existing infrastructure, and addressing data privacy concerns. In conclusion, leveraging AI for crack detection and maintenance in building infrastructure represents a significant step forward in ensuring structural safety and operational efficiency. This paper provides insights into the current state of AI applications in this field and offers recommendations for future research and development. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Digital-Twin-Based Modeling and Fault Prediction Method for Industrial Robots
titulo_norm: digital twin based modeling and fault prediction method for industrial robots
resumo: Fault prediction technology anticipates potential failures by examining operational data of equipment and developing deep learning models. These techniques are extensively applied in the realm of electromechanical equipment within the manufacturing industry to facilitate proactive maintenance, minimize downtime, and enhance equipment dependability. Nevertheless, within intricate engineering domains such as six-axis industrial robots, traditional prediction techniques may encounter an overwhelming computational burden and exhibit subpar performance in terms of predictive accuracy. In this study, the authors introduce the Lagrangian convolutional long short-term memory neural network (LC-LSTM) as a novel approach for predicting faults in industrial robots. By combining a convolutional neural network with a long short-term memory network (LSTM), the LC-LSTM model can effectively analyze the temporal data collected from individual axes. This integration allows for independent prediction of the rotation angle and torque for each axis. The enhanced Lagrangian neural network is not only applicable for elucidating the dynamics and kinematics of robotic arms but also for directly modeling the correlation between force and motion. Consequently, it can more accurately forecast parameters such as force, velocity, and acceleration for individual axes of industrial robots. After training 2660 sets of data containing various faults, the LC-LSTM model demonstrates the capability to predict distinct faults for each axis of industrial robots with an average accuracy of 95.45%, an average recall ratio of 95.58%, and an average precision ratio of 94.8%. In addition, this study introduces a digital twin model (DTM) for industrial robots, which combines predictive modeling with digital twin technology to facilitate real-time monitoring and accurate tracking of equipment operational status. This methodology enables more precise failure forecasts, consequently improving the general dependability and effectiveness of the machinery. Subsequently, a reinforcement learning model is suggested to adjust the twin's parameters, guaranteeing a significant level of coherence between the DTM and the actual system as time progresses. To evaluate the dependability of the DTM, we confirmed its ability to autonomously update parameters. The state of the twin model, trained on 200 datasets, is observed during different fault incidents, achieving an average accuracy of 91.4%. © 2020 IEEE.

titulo_norm: digital twins and ai for predictive maintenance of renewable energy assets

It also discusses the uses of DTs and AI in predictive maintenance of renewable energy assets with some backgrounds integration schemes, industrial practices, examples of their application, challenges, and future prospects of introducing smarter, resilient and more sustainable energy system. The DT-AI framework brings together the process of acquisition, communication, storage, simulation and AI modeling to make it feasible to facilitate end-to-end predictive maintenance. The suggested system combines the IoT-based data collection, feature extraction with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and fault classification with the help of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. Significant improvement is shown by experimental evaluation with the accuracy of 97.4 and fault detection rate of 98.1 and also reduction of maintenance costs by 44.2 percent as compared to that of traditional systems. The data on vibration was evaluated to determine the trends in terms of bearing faults, shaft imbalance, and wear in gears, which are efficient in the prediction of failures prior to the catastrophic breakdowns. titulo: Enhancing Industrial Automation Through IIoT-Enabled Cloud Computing and LSTM for Scalable and Real-Time Data Analytics
titulo_norm: enhancing industrial automation through iiot enabled cloud computing and lstm for scalable and real time data analytics
resumo: In this thesis, we investigate the combined application of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), cloud computing and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to facilitate advanced industrial automation through the industrial analytics enabled by scalable and real time data processing. IIoT is an industrial approach to generating very large amounts of data from connected industrial devices that can be parsed through cloud computing to yield immediate insights into production processes, equipment health, and operational efficiency. Since this is a time series data, we employ LSTM (A type of recurrent neural network) in this architecture which is able to handle time series data well and is a good fit for predictive maintenance and anomaly detection problems in industrial setting. The proposed system involves three main components: Second, the IoT collection of data from IIoT devices, storage of data in the cloud, and processing of data are stored in the cloud; and finally, real time analysis of data using LSTM models. The LSTM models train on historical datasets containing sensor readings and machine logs, to make accurate equipment failure and process optimization predictions. For large scale data processing we use cloud computing platforms like AWS or Azure to manage where these big databases are located. Evaluation of the system performance is presented in the study with regard to prediction accuracy, latency and a comparison of LSTM with other ML techniques. We can see that that there's strong potential for these technologies to have a powerful impact on industrial automation, downtime, and operational efficiency. Yet, there are still data security and system scalability issues to explore. This research shows that IIoT implants and cloud computing, in conjunction with LSTM, can be designed to transform existing production processes. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: ESP32 as a Dual-Connectivity Data Logger: Exploring GSM and Wi-Fi Integration for IoT

resumo: The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) necessitates dependable and adaptable data collection systems to enable real-time analytics and decision-making. This paper investigates the use of ESP32 as a dual-connectivity data logger, combining GSM and Wi-Fi communication to facilitate seamless data acquisition and transmission for AI-driven IoT applications. Wi-Fi enables faster and more cost-effective data transfer in networked areas, whereas GSM connectivity ensures reliable operation in remote or off-grid environments. This hybrid approach improves the performance of AI models in predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and smart agriculture by ensuring continuous and high-quality data flow. This study presents the system description and performance of a data logger using an ESP32 microcontroller that works with WiFi and GSM connectivity. The results show that the ESP32 microcontroller with Wi-Fi connectivity transmits data quickly and consistently, resulting in a higher success rate, whereas GSM connectivity ensures that data is logged even in areas with intermittent or no Wi-Fi. The results demonstrate the benefits of dual connectivity in terms of data reliability, accessibility, and AI integration. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: SVM-based Vibration Analysis for Early Fault Detection in Industrial Rotating Machines
titulo_norm: svm based vibration analysis for early fault detection in industrial rotating machines
resumo: The prompt identification of defects in industrial rotating equipment is essential to save unforeseen downtime and maintenance expenses. Traditional threshold-based vibration monitoring techniques often experience delayed detection and increased false alarm rates. This work introduces a Support Vector Machine (SVM) methodology for the early identification of faults using vibration data obtained from accelerometers. Features were derived from both time and frequency domains to identify critical features of mechanical abnormalities, including bearing failures, misalignment, and imbalance. The proposed SVM model was trained and verified on an industrial vibration dataset, with an accuracy of 98.4% in fault classification. The deployment of an IoT-enabled monitoring platform facilitated real-time data analysis, resulting in a 23.5% reduction in false positives and an 18.7% enhancement in early failure detection relative to traditional approaches. Computational efficiency was assessed, revealing an inference time of 3.4 ms per sample, hence validating its appropriateness for real-time implementation. The findings indicate that SVM-based vibration analysis provides a dependable, precise, and effective approach for predictive maintenance, improving equipment dependability, operational safety, and overall industrial productivity. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Development of advanced intrusion detection approach using machine and ensemble learning for industrial internet of things networks
titulo_norm: development of advanced intrusion detection approach using machine and ensemble learning for industrial internet of things networks
resumo: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks plays a significant role in enhancing industrial automation systems by connecting industrial devices for real time data monitoring and predictive maintenance. However, this connectivity introduces new vulnerabilities which demand the development of advanced intrusion detection systems. The nuclear facilities are considered one of the closest examples of critical infrastructures that suffer from high vulnerability through the connectivity of IIoT networks. This paper develops a robust intrusion detection approach using machine and ensemble learning algorithms specifically determined for IIoT networks. This approach can achieve optimal performance with low time complexity suitable for real-time IIoT networks. For each algorithm, Grid Search is determined to fine-tune the hyperparameters for optimizing the performance while ensuring time computational efficiency. The proposed approach is investigated on recent IIoT intrusion detection datasets, WUSTL-IIOT-2021 and Edge-IIoT-2022 to cover a wider range of attacks with high precision and minimum false alarms. The study provides the effectiveness of ten machine and ensemble learning models on selected features of the datasets. Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE)-based multi-class balancing is used to manipulate dataset imbalances. The ensemble voting classifier is used to combine the best models with the best hyperparameters for raising their advantages to improve the performance with the least time complexity. The machine and ensemble learning algorithms are evaluated based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1 Score, and time complexity. This evaluation can discriminate the most suitable candidates for further optimization. The proposed approach is called the XCL approach that is based on Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), CatBoost (Categorical Boosting), and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM). It achieves high accuracy, lower false positive rate, and efficient time complexity. The results refer to the importance of ensemble strategies, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter optimization in enhancing the performance to detect the different intrusions across the IIoT datasets over the other models. The developed approach produced a higher accuracy of 99.99 % on the WUSTL-IIOT-2021 dataset and 100 % on the Edge-IIoTset dataset. Our experimental evaluations have been extended to the CIC-IDS-2017 dataset. These additional evaluations not only highlight the applicability of the XCL approach on a wide spectrum of intrusion detection scenarios but also confirm its scalability and effectiveness in real-world complex network environments. © 2025 Mohamed I. titulo: Event-Based Data in Prognostics and Health Management: A Systematic Review of Models, Challenges, and Applications
titulo_norm: event based data in prognostics and health management a systematic review of models challenges and applications
resumo: In the modern industrial context, Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) systems based on data-driven approaches have been widely and effectively developed to reduce maintenance costs. However, continuous data requires large memory capacity and high costs. Therefore, in recent years, the use of event-based data for PHM models has become prominent and increasingly attracts attention due to its cost-efficiency and effectiveness. This surge in data availability has opened new avenues for developing datadriven methods that leverage event patterns to enhance diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive maintenance capabilities. Building meaningful and interpretable patterns from raw event data is crucial for understanding system behavior, detecting faults early, forecasting future failures, and accurately estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of critical components. This review paper systematically surveys the state-of-the-art methodologies and frameworks for extracting, modeling, and utilizing event-based patterns in the context of diagnostic and prognostic applications. Furthermore, we analyze challenges related to event data heterogeneity, scalability, and interpretability, as well as the need for robust pattern extraction methods that can adapt to dynamic operating environments. The review further explores how these event-based patterns contribute to building reliable diagnostic models, enabling early fault detection, and supporting maintenance decision-making through precise prognostics. Finally, this paper identifies key research gaps and outlines future directions, emphasizing the need for explainable, adaptive, and scalable pattern mining approaches that effectively translate raw event data into actionable maintenance intelligence. To tackle thesechallenges, we propose a unified pattern construction framework general event pattern for diagnostic, prognostic, and RUL prediction tasks, designed to be adaptable across diverse industrial systems. This comprehensive survey aims to serve as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners committed to leveraging event data for enhanced system reliability and the development of optimized, intelligent maintenance strategies. © 2025, Prognostics and Health Management Society. This work presents an IoT-based remote monitoring system for blowers in wastewater treatment plants, utilizing a Total Degradation Number (TDN) sensor for oil condition assessment, existing vibration sensors, and oil temperature monitoring.The system continuously tracks critical blower parameters, including the TDN to evaluate oil degradation, oil temperature, vibration levels, and operational runtime. By applying high-frequency AC waveforms, the TDN sensor accurately measures oil capacitance and conductance, deriving the TDN as a simplified index of oil health. Sensor data is seamlessly collected, transmitted to a cloud platform, and displayed on an intuitive dashboard that provides real-time visualization and automated alerts for abnormal conditions.Field testing in an operational wastewater treatment facility demonstrates the system's effectiveness in early fault detection, reducing unexpected failures, and optimizing maintenance schedules. This paper introduces a smart IoT-based system that is meant to avoid short circuits during the EV charging operation while also supporting early-time scheduling to make better use of energy and grid load. The system suggested here keeps a constant check on the charging parameters like voltage, current, and temperature through real-time sensors. On detecting abnormal readings or faults, the system automatically switches off the power supply to avoid short circuits and maintain vehicle safety. Furthermore, a scheduling algorithm is employed to calculate the most appropriate times for charging based on energy demand and availability. The system utilizes cloud connectivity to provide remote monitoring and alert notifications through an easy-to- use interface. titulo: IP-aware Federated Manufacturing Intelligence
titulo_norm: ip aware federated manufacturing intelligence
resumo: The application of deep learning in semiconductor manufacturing holds great promise but faces significant challenges, particularly in safeguarding intellectual property (IP) during data exchanges. Consider a scenario where the same equipment is deployed across multiple manufacturers. Equipment providers need to collect operational data to offer continuous service improvements, while manufacturers must balance the utility of shared data with the risk of IP leakage. This challenge is compounded by the opacity of deep learning models, raising the question: how can manufacturers ensure their sensitive data remains protected? We address this issue with the IP-aware Federated Manufacturing Intelligence (IPFMI) framework, a novel distributed learning architecture designed to ensure IP protection in federated learning (FL) settings. In IPFMI, data collected by Remote Equipment (RE) at each Semiconductor Manufacturer (SM) undergoes an IP-preserving transformation before being shared with a centralized Service Architect (SA). The SA aggregates this sanitized data to train a central model, enabling performance improvements such as predictive maintenance, process optimization, and anomaly detection without accessing raw data. This approach strikes a balance between utility and privacy, facilitating secure, privacy-preserving collaboration between manufacturers and equipment providers. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Synergy of AI and IoT in Water Monitoring

resumo: Traditional water quality monitoring (WQM) methods are labor-intensive and time-consuming, and lack of real-time abilities. IoT-based systems integrate advanced sensors, cloud computing, and wireless communication technologies, which ensure real-time data collection, future stating analysis, and efficient water management. This chapter examines the role of architecture, data collection strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI) in IoT-enabled WQM. The proposed system includes the upper and lower tank monitoring units that communicate virally through the 2.4 GHz RF module. The upper unit ESP8266 transmits real-time data to the cloud using the Wi-Fi module, while the lower unit controls the water supply through a relay-based pump system. Efficient communication protocols such as LPWAN and 5G enhance scalability and power efficiency, making the system suitable for mass deployment.Major sensor technologies, including pH sensor, turbidity sensor, flow sensor, and DS18B20 temperature sensors, provide precise readings important to assess water quality. titulo: Vibration-Based Failure Prediction in Machinery: Novel Application of Time Series Decomposition and Neural Networks
titulo_norm: vibration based failure prediction in machinery novel application of time series decomposition and neural networks
resumo: Predictive maintenance (PdM) is critical in reducing downtime and minimizing operational costs in industrial settings. This study introduces a novel framework for vibration-based failure prediction by combining Seasonal and Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL) and deep learning models, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The framework processes multivariate vibration data collected from two-roller mills in a tire manufacturing facility. STL is employed to decompose the data into trend, seasonal, and residual components, enabling noise reduction and enhanced feature extraction. These components serve as inputs to LSTM models for predicting machine condition scores. A comprehensive analysis compared five deep learning architectures: LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Deeper LSTM, and Conv1D LSTM. The GRU and Conv1D LSTM demonstrated superior performance across multiple vibration axes, achieving low errors and high R2 values. Results highlight the effectiveness of STL in preparing vibration data for sequential learning and the robust predictive capabilities of deep learning models. This study provides a scalable approach to PdM, enhancing reliability and efficiency in industrial machinery maintenance. Future work includes extending the framework to other machinery types and real-time monitoring systems.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Digital Twin for Industrial Workplace Safety

Key functionalities include real-time data acquisition from IoT integrated sensors, which facilitate continuous monitoring of operational conditions and environmental factors. AI-driven analytics within DT support predictive maintenance, hazard identification, and anomaly detection, thereby preemptively addressing potential safety risks. titulo: Predicting Insufficient Oil vs Insufficient Refrigerant for Belt-Driven Air Conditioning Compressor using Z-Chart
titulo_norm: predicting insufficient oil vs insufficient refrigerant for belt driven air conditioning compressor using z chart
resumo: Air conditioning (A/C) systems are critical for ensuring driver and passenger comfort, especially during long journeys, where the compressor serves as the core component. The reliability of a belt-driven A/C compressor largely depends on maintaining optimal oil and refrigerant levels. However, deficiencies in fluid can lead to significant compressor damage, reduced cooling performance, and compromised cabin comfort. Conventional diagnostic approaches, especially for monitoring oil levels, often prove inadequate, leading to misdiagnosis and suboptimal maintenance decisions. This research introduces a vibration-based diagnostic approach using Z-Chart analysis to predict insufficient or excessive oil and refrigerant conditions in belt-driven swash plate-type compressors. Controlled laboratory experiments were conducted by systematically varying oil and refrigerant levels. Vibration signals were captured using a tri-axial accelerometer and processed via Z-freq 3D, a frequency-domain technique based on the Integrated Kurtosis algorithm. The Z-Chart was constructed by analysing the b/a coefficient derived from the exponential fit of Z-freq 3D data across different compressor speeds. Findings reveal that the Z-Chart method effectively differentiates between underfilled and overfilled oil and refrigerant states, enabling early fault detection before significant degradation occurs. This technique represents a novel and practical advancement for condition monitoring, aligning with the goals of predictive maintenance and enhanced occupant comfort. Its application is particularly relevant in the automotive and HVAC sectors, offering improved diagnostic reliability and reduced risk of incorrect service actions.  © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

titulo: Optimizing Manufacturing Efficiency: A Hybrid ML and DL Model for Predictive Maintenance

resumo: With the advent of Industry 4.0 and the incorporation of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) into production, PdM has grown more important in a number of industries. These systems provide independent, adaptable production settings and provide significant cost advantages. Key performance indicators (KPIs) must be in place to support a modular and scalable PdM architecture for implementation to be effective. Data normalisation is the first step in this study's advanced PdM technique, which aims to guarantee consistency within specified parameters. Hierarchical clustering based on correlation and relative entropy, as evaluated by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, are used to extract a subset of features with smaller dimensions. The input data is analysed for seasonality and geographical relationships using a CNN, while the temporal dependencies are captured using a BiLSTM network. The suggested CNBiAM model relies on an AM to adaptively improve the BiLSTM according to the input sequence, allowing for even more precise predictions. In comparison to more conventional models, CNBiAM outperforms them computationally, with a forecasting accuracy of 96.81%. Modern automated production settings rely on predictive maintenance systems, and these results show that clever DL frameworks are the key to keeping them robust and accurate. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Meta-Learning-Based Domain Generalization for Cost-Effective Tool Condition Monitoring in Ultrasonic Metal Welding
titulo_norm: meta learning based domain generalization for cost effective tool condition monitoring in ultrasonic metal welding
resumo: Online tool condition monitoring (TCM) is a pivotal capability in many manufacturing applications including ultrasonic metal welding (UMW). Effective and efficient TCM can facilitate predictive maintenance, improve product quality, and enhance productivity. Existing online TCM systems based on conventional machine learning models often require a large amount of labeled data, the collection of which is cost-prohibitive, time-consuming, and labor-intensive. Such models fail to satisfy the requirements of cost-effectiveness and agility posed by modern, reconfigurable UMW systems. As such, data-efficient TCM methods with excellent generalization ability are of vital importance. To this end, we develop a novel similarity-based meta-representation learning (SMRL) method for domain generalization. SMRL effectively learns high-level meta-knowledge that is shared among different welding scenarios or domains. Therefore, the model trained in source domains can be generalized to other domains without access to labeled data in the training phase. Case studies are performed using four welding scenarios with varied welding materials and welding parameters. It is demonstrated that the proposed method is superior to the baseline methods, including neural network, hierarchical neural network, model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), and hierarchical MAML. Compared with the baseline methods, SMRL offers an average improvement of 15.44%-31.62% in TCM accuracy. These results show that SMRL is readily applicable to industrial applications to enable cost-effective and data-efficient TCM.  © 2005-2012 IEEE.

titulo: ACSA: A Hybrid Approach for Designing Smart Building Maintenance Strategies
titulo_norm: acsa a hybrid approach for designing smart building maintenance strategies
resumo: Effective Predictive Maintenance is essential for ensuring the reliability of Smart Building systems while minimizing maintenance costs. This paper explores maintenance optimization by modeling system interactions using a Fault Tree and characterizing component failures with Weibull distributions. We evaluate two optimization techniques to enhance decision-making in this complex environment: Reinforcement Learning and Simulated Annealing. We propose ACSA, a hybrid algorithm that integrates reinforcement learning (Actor-Critic) with stochastic optimization (Simulated Annealing) to adjust maintenance strategies dynamically. Experimental results show that ACSA achieves a superior balance between system reliability and intervention costs while meeting Quality of Service constraints. This hybrid approach leverages adaptive decision-making to efficiently manage maintenance in non-stationary environments, making it a scalable solution for interconnected systems or any system of systems. © 2025 RQD. titulo: Intelligent Decision Support System Based on BIM in Power Grid Engineering
titulo_norm: intelligent decision support system based on bim in power grid engineering
resumo: The popularization and in-depth application of Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology have greatly promoted the improvement of building operation and maintenance management efficiency. BIM not only provides unprecedented accuracy for cost estimation by constructing high-precision 3D models, but also achieves deep optimization of resource allocation and cost control, effectively strengthening collaborative operations and information flow among project participants. BIM technology can reflect project changes in real time, significantly improving the response speed and processing efficiency of project change management, ensuring that the project can proceed smoothly according to established goals. In response to the complex planning and difficult decision-making of power grid engineering projects, this paper designs an intelligent decision support system for power grid engineering projects based on BIM. This system deeply integrates the spatial analysis capabilities of BIM technology, the massive data processing capabilities of big data technology, and the intelligent decision-making capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, aiming to achieve comprehensive, accurate, and efficient planning and management of power grid engineering projects. The experimental results show that the system can significantly improve the planning efficiency and quality of power grid engineering projects, providing decision-makers with more scientific, reasonable, and feasible solution choices.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Enhancing Residential Gas Safety through Remote Monitoring and Embedded Microchip Systems
titulo_norm: enhancing residential gas safety through remote monitoring and embedded microchip systems
resumo: Residential use of combustible gases (for example, LPG or natural gas) creates several safety issues, as missed leaks can result in fires, explosions, and harm or death. Relying on simple conventional detectors or inspecting manually is usually insufficient to protect a site. The paper proposes an entirely innovative gas safety system that integrates sensing with embedded microcontrollers, wireless monitoring, and automated actuation enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) at the edge. The system combines low-cost semiconductor gas sensors such as MQ-series gas sensors with an Arduino or NodeMCU microchip to regularly measure the gas concentration. A lightweight machine learning model runs locally on the device, enabling accurate anomaly detection while reducing false positives caused by environmental fluctuations. When levels exceed a safe threshold, the system sounds a local alarm, activates a shut-off valve, and immediately transmits an alert to remote users via IoT (for example, Wi-Fi/cloud and SMS) for rapid intervention. The system alarms locally when gas concentration levels reach dangerous levels, operates a shut-off valve, and alarms remotely via Wi-Fi or GSM to enable user action within a reasonable time frame. The cloud maintains a digital twist of the system, which provides the system with real-Time synchronization, predictive maintenance, and historical analytics. The communication is strong due to multi-network support, such as Wi-Fi, GSM, and optional LoRaWAN. The security protocols, including encrypted MQTT protocols and blockchain anchoring of event logs, provide traceability and data integrity. The paper also examines prevailing gas-monitoring technologies and shows our prototype's design approach, outlining the sensors, microcontroller, and communication used. The suggested architecture (shown in Fig. 1) uses local processing and a connection to the cloud to ensure round-The-clock monitoring. We examine how different sensors perform and what problems they may have, and we offer helpful advice for their future development. The proposed solution is based on AI and the IoT, and it aims to be scalable, power-efficient, and smart-home-integrated to improve the safety of residents and industries using gas with a practical and future-oriented solution.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Multi-Model Machine Learning Framework for Smart Vehicle Telemetry Analytics
titulo_norm: multi model machine learning framework for smart vehicle telemetry analytics
resumo: This article suggests using machine learning algorithms to analyze car telemetry data for predicting maintenance needs, understanding driver behavior, and assessing risks in connected vehicles. The system uses several machine learning techniques, such as Random Forest for predicting warning codes, Linear Regression for forecasting fuel economy, K-Means for segmenting drivers, Isolation Forest for detecting anomalies, and Decision Trees for assessing driver risk. Testing is carried out using simulated car data that simulates real-time inputs like speed, RPM, engine temperature, fuel usage, and brake pressure. Together with such methods, the system can detect maintenance errors and divide drivers into individual behavior patterns. The results show that Random Forest is the best model to use when predicting warning codes, and K-Means effectively clusters the drivers based on their behavior Isolation Forest assists in identifying potential maintenance issues by locating anomalies, and Decision Trees are precise in differentiating between safe and dangerous drivers. These techniques combined provide an automotive analytics solution that aids in the creation of intelligent car systems, enhancing safety and efficiency. Real-time applications using IoT devices will be pursued in future work, as well as deep learning for improved predictions. This framework moves the auto IoT idea closer to facilitating automated decision-making using data.  © 2025 IEEE.
