titulo: Building trust by design through explainable AI for resilient and cognitive smart grids
titulo_norm: building trust by design through explainable ai for resilient and cognitive smart grids
resumo: Traditional electrical power grids have historically faced challenges with operational reliability, stability, flexibility, and efficiency. Machine learning (ML) aids in enhancing smart grids (SGs) by enabling predictive maintenance, optimizing energy distribution, and ensuring efficient and stable grid operations. Despite the ubiquitousness of ML methods, these methods lack transparency and explainability for SG applications due to their non-linear multilayer structures. Thus, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) emerged as the missing piece toward human-centered AI that prioritizes the humanistic design perspective. This study aims to explore the potential of XAI for SGs. A background review of the explainability paradigm and its urgent need for SGs is provided. In addition, multiple XAI models are discussed while citing their advantages and drawbacks. Next, the chapter discusses a wide spectrum of SG-based XAI applications. This chapter promotes the exploration of the emerging XAI paradigms, specifically for SG applications. With this study, the authors hope that this work will serve as a touchstone for theorists and practitioners alike, promoting trust in AI systems through enhanced transparency and ultimately enhancing the resilience of SGs. © The Institution of Engineering and Technology and its licensors 2025.

titulo: AI-Powered Predictive Maintenance for Field Equipment Optimization and Failure Risk Reduction
titulo_norm: ai powered predictive maintenance for field equipment optimization and failure risk reduction
resumo: Failures of field equipment often result in expensive downtime and reduced production in industrial and agricultural operations. This research introduces an AI-driven predictive maintenance system using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to enhance equipment efficiency and mitigate failure risks. IoT-enabled sensors constantly monitor critical characteristics like temperature, vibration, and pressure. The LSTM model analyses the gathered time-series data, which is trained on past maintenance and failure records. The method was implemented on a dataset of equipment operating cycles, with a prediction accuracy of 94.7% for possible failures. The LSTM-based method decreased unscheduled downtime by 38% and maintenance expenses by 27% compared to traditional scheduled maintenance. Moreover, the lifespan of equipment improved by 15% due to prompt intervention. The model had a precision of 93.82% and a recall of 95.37%, indicating dependable early failure identification. The findings validate the efficacy of LSTM in predictive maintenance, facilitating data-driven decision-making and operational resilience in field settings with minimum human involvement.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: CO2- and PM2.5-Focused Optimal Ventilation Strategy Based on Predictive Control
titulo_norm: co2 and pm2 5 focused optimal ventilation strategy based on predictive control
resumo: This study developed and evaluated an optimal ventilation strategy for variable air volume (VAV) systems, targeting carbon dioxide (CO2) and particulate matter less than 2.5 μm in diameter (PM2.5) concentrations. The strategy integrates system-level demand-controlled ventilation (DCV) based on real-time occupancy data and zone-level predictive control using indoor air quality (IAQ) prediction models. By predicting indoor CO2 and PM2.5 levels for the subsequent time step and dynamically adjusting control priorities, optimal airflow is determined. A co-simulation model integrating EnergyPlus, CONTAM, and Python was employed for model training and testing. The proposed strategy was compared with on–off control, CO2 predictive control, and PM2.5 predictive control, demonstrating superior prediction accuracy and stable IAQ maintenance. The optimal ventilation strategy achieved the highest performance, maintaining CO2 and PM2.5 levels below their respective upper limits of 100% and 97.33% of the time. Although this strategy resulted in slightly higher energy consumption compared to the other control algorithms due to its multivariable control approach, it effectively maintained IAQ standards. This method simplifies development and maintenance by circumventing the need for complex optimization, providing a flexible and cost-effective solution for IAQ management. Future research will focus on developing integrated VAV system control strategies that ensure comfort year-round, addressing both energy efficiency and thermal comfort. titulo: Strategic Implementation of AI for Business Advancement
titulo_norm: strategic implementation of ai for business advancement
resumo: New-era artificial intelligence (AI) has become essential for businesses to improve overall efficiency. AI works as a tool that can help the organization automate time-consuming tasks, for example, in businesses, intelligent document processing is the full automation of document-based workflow using AI technologies. It also gains insights from huge volumes of documents, and AI provides various facilities for companies - customer service chatbots, predictive analysis, sales forecasting, fraud detection, etc. AI helps both parts of businesses and customers with everyday transactions, and the objective of this study is to understand how to strategically implement AI for business advancement. The successful AI strategic implementation should act as a roadmap for the plan. It depends on the business goals and the steps for appropriate use of AI to extract insights from data, create a better supply chain, enhance efficiency and ecosystem, and improve talent and customer experience. Businesses integrating AI benefit from various advantages, particularly improved productivity and enhanced decision-making processes. The chapter also explains the steps for building a successful AI strategy to gain understanding of generative AI, natural language processing, ML, and computer vision. AI adoption is not a meager technological upgrade but rather a major strategic upgrade that can help businesses move forward at a better step and provide tangible benefits in businesses, including revenue growth and data-driven decision-making. AI plays a crucial role in increasing business efficiency and productivity, providing quick responses, freeing humans, and handling more complex issues. AI not only reduces operational costs but also ensures a unified and responsive experience for customers, which means improving overall efficiency of the business, and with the help of AI, companies gain sustainable competitive advantages. Leveraging technologies enables businesses to anticipate market trends, optimize operations, and respond quickly to customers’ needs. Businesses identify new product ideas with the help of AI, and on the other hand, streamline the research and development processes and improve product quality through predictive maintenance and faster innovation. There are some factors to consider while selecting the AI model for the business: data type, problem complexity, labeled data availability, computational resources, and interpretability needs. AI refers to the simulation of human types of intelligence in machines, which is implemented by specific tasks such as collecting data and performing relevant data processing, selecting suitable AI models, and integrating them into the system. Implementation of AI has many potential downfalls to consider: the security of AI has been the major concern among the business community. AI is an additional level of technology, and while using AI in businesses, make sure to select a platform or a business service with the necessary security to keep all data safe and secure. titulo: Federated Learning for Geothermal Energy: A Decentralized Solution for Data Sharing and Sector Learning
titulo_norm: federated learning for geothermal energy a decentralized solution for data sharing and sector learning
resumo: Geothermal energy faces challenges in design and operation due to subsurface uncertainties, high drilling costs, and complex maintenance requirements. Data and model sharing can enhance decision making processes in the geothermal sector by improving predictive maintenance, equipment and production monitoring during the operation to explore and design new geothermal installations by enabling advanced analytics and collaborative insights. However, concerns over data privacy and proprietary information hinder widespread adoption. This paper explores federated learning (FL) as a decentralized machine learning approach that facilitates secure collaboration across geothermal sites without sharing raw data. By aggregating model updates, FL improves anomaly detection, downtime reduction, and cost efficiency while preserving confidentiality. A case study demonstrates its effectiveness in predictive maintenance. The results showed that the FL models have a significantly higher accuracy and generalization compared to individual model of each stakeholder. The added value of FL models is more dominant for the parties with limited or small data. Findings highlight FL's potential to foster collaboration among operators, manufacturers, and researchers, enabling privacy-preserving, data-driven optimization in geothermal energy. titulo: Challenges and Opportunities in AI-Driven Supply Chain Sustainability: A Review Article
titulo_norm: challenges and opportunities in ai driven supply chain sustainability a review article
resumo: This tries to review challenges and opportunities in AI-driven supply chain sustainability comprehensively. Thus, qualitative research aims to study the implications and possibilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies associated with supply chain sustainability (SCS). Sustainability is one of the most crucial components of modern ethical and social practices due to environmental problems, such as global warming and resource depletion. At the same time, SCS is applied to attain economic sustainability and maintain competitive business models with environmental and social responsibility. The AI technologies can project demands, record optimization, predictive maintenance, and supplier risk management to facilitate supply chain operations. So, AI significantly optimizes supply chain operations by facilitating decision-making processes and saving suppliers’ and customers’ time and money. However, the trained AI model could be unfair or unethical and may lack transparency and accountability, thereby raising the privacy issues of both suppliers and customers. The integration of AI technologies into SCS also presents several opportunities for organizations. For instance, demand forecasting may be enhanced with AI by using historical data to predict trends in business, which will affect inventory handling. It will allow the avoidance of overstock situations and stockout shelves, subsequently saving costs and inventory wastage for organizations. Another important aspect is that the production demand fluctuations for a particular product could be predicted, and adequate inventory levels could be maintained. It is also helpful for better management of sourcing and supplier relations. It will help organizations to pursue ‘green’ sourcing practices, rely on more ethical sourcing solutions, and optimize their supply chains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Optimizing Energy Storage, Performance Monitoring, and Predictive Maintenance Through the Integration of IIoT and Battery Management Systems
titulo_norm: optimizing energy storage performance monitoring and predictive maintenance through the integration of iiot and battery management systems
resumo: Rapid advancements in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Battery Management Systems (BMS) have opened up new possibilities for intelligent energy storage, better performance tracking, and predictive maintenance. This study explores how HoT-enabled sensors, cloud computing, and ML algorithms can be all integrated within BMS for maintaining better energy storage efficiency and system reliability. The framework maximizes real-time data acquisition and advanced analytics for accurate estimates of state-of-charge (SoC), state-of-health (SoH), fault detection, and performance diagnostics. The system enables adaptive energy management to help maximize the lifespan of batteries while minimizing energy losses and downtime. On top of that, IIoT connectivity facilitates remote monitoring and control at scale, enabling industries to improve efficiency and sustainability. Safety and reliability are essential in any battery management system, and one of its primary challenges is to maximize energy storage efficiency. The study also examines predictive maintenance techniques that use machine learning and artificial intelligence to predict upcoming failures and optimize maintenance scheduling. The value of ML comes from its ability to analyze historical and real-time operational data to identify anomalies and predict battery degradation patterns so that proactive interventions can be undertaken. Additionally, secure cloud storage, edge computing, and data encryption mechanisms are investigated to maintain data integrity, low-latency processing, and cybersecurity resilience in industrial settings. This continues on in the most widely applicable findings of the research where HoT and BMS are found as converged entities, which collectively improves the energy storage functionalities but also makes the battery management as a data driven intelligent decision making process. This advancement will transform industrial power systems, electric mobility, and renewable energy storage systems by increasing resource efficiency and decreasing operating risks.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life of Railway Wheels: A Data-Driven Approach for Predictive Maintenance
titulo_norm: predicting the remaining useful life of railway wheels a data driven approach for predictive maintenance
resumo: Building on previous work on wear law modeling, this paper focuses on the prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of a complex system, whose state is characterized by multivariate time-series data. Our study is framed within the context of predictive maintenance applied to rolling stock, particularly railway wheels. We propose an approach to estimate future wear based on the wear law, while using the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction as a key performance indicator. We also evaluate the accuracy and reliability of the prediction model. We demonstrate the performance of RUL predictions for three factors (Flange height, Flange width, Flange gradient), with improvements of up to 8% in the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for Flange width, a 60% gain for Flange height, and 32% for Flange gradient. These results highlight the generalizability and relevance of our approach.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: M2AD: Multi-Sensor Multi-System Anomaly Detection through Global Scoring and Calibrated Thresholding
titulo_norm: m2ad multi sensor multi system anomaly detection through global scoring and calibrated thresholding
resumo: With the widespread availability of sensor data across industrial and operational systems, we frequently encounter heterogeneous time series from multiple systems. Anomaly detection is crucial for such systems to facilitate predictive maintenance. However, most existing anomaly detection methods are designed for either univariate or single-system multivariate data, making them insufficient for these complex scenarios. To address this, we introduce M2AD, a framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series data from multiple systems. M2AD employs deep models to capture expected behavior under normal conditions, using the residuals as indicators of potential anomalies. These residuals are then aggregated into a global anomaly score through a Gaussian Mixture Model and Gamma calibration. We theoretically demonstrate that this framework can effectively address heterogeneity and dependencies across sensors and systems. Empirically, M2AD outperforms existing methods in extensive evaluations by 21% on average, and its effectiveness is demonstrated on a large-scale real-world case study on 130 assets in Amazon Fulfillment Centers. Our code and results are available at https://github.com/sarahmish/M2AD. Copyright 2025 by the author(s).

titulo: AI and Data Science for Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0
titulo_norm: ai and data science for predictive maintenance in industry 4 0
resumo: Under Industry 4.0, predictive maintenance has been a key requirement in reducing downtime and maximizing asset performance across sophisticated industrial systems. The proposed research suggests an integrated AI-based framework combining conventional machine learning (ML) techniques (Random Forest, SVM) with deep learning (DL) architectures (CNN, LSTM) and XAI methods like SHAP to ensure transparency and stakeholder confidence. Preprocessed time-series Sensor data from industrial machinery was used to train prediction models for malfunction detection and estimating the remaining useful life (RUL). Real-time deployment was implemented using edge computing to reduce latency and facilitate timely decision-making. Results showed that the LSTM model provided the best performance with 91% precision, 88% recall, and 82.1% RUL accuracy. When combined with SHAP, the model had high accuracy (90% precision, 87% recall) and provided better interpretability. Our work emphasizes the interpretability-latency trade-off since the XAI-enhanced model exhibited a marginally higher latency (110 ms). Nevertheless, the paradigm was successful in providing accurate, real-time, and interpretable predictions. The drawbacks are added computational overhead and the requirement for large-scale labeled data. Follow-on work will prioritize minimizing XAI latency, making data more efficient, and evaluating federated and privacy-preserving learning approaches. This system improves the transparency and trustworthiness of AI applications in industrial predictive maintenance.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Cognitive Digital Twins: Integrating Deep Learning Models for Proactive Facilities Management in Smart Buildings
titulo_norm: cognitive digital twins integrating deep learning models for proactive facilities management in smart buildings
resumo: Digital twins (DTs) are revolutionizing the AECO industry by offering real-time digital replicas of physical assets. However, the integration of continuous, automated predictive forecasts within DTs remains limited. A framework that integrates AI and ML technologies with operational DTs was developed and implemented, enabling predictive capabilities. Using a Long Short-Term Memory neural network, daily energy consumption was predicted based on historical energy usage and real-time weather forecasts. The model achieved an MAE of 178.79 kWh, a root RMSE of 236.02 kWh, and an MAPE of 2.98%, demonstrating its ability to generalize while capturing seasonal and operational trends. By functioning as predictive systems, DTs transform into comprehensive common data environments (CDEs) that aggregate and contextualize data, empowering stakeholders with actionable insights. This framework not only demonstrates practical applicability but also lays the foundation for cognitive digital twins (CDTs), enabling them to evolve into intelligent, adaptive systems for smarter, more sustainable building operations. © ASCE.

titulo: Estimation of Bridge Girder Cumulative Displacement for Component Operational Warning Using Bayesian Neural Networks
titulo_norm: estimation of bridge girder cumulative displacement for component operational warning using bayesian neural networks
resumo: The main girders of suspension bridges experience significant deformation due to temperature variations, wind dynamics, and vehicle loads, causing movement at the girder ends and friction among components such as bearings, expansion joints, and viscous dampers. Early warning of the component anomaly is vital for preventive maintenance. This paper develops a two-stage framework for predicting girder end displacement to facilitate anomaly detection. First, a Bayesian neural network is employed to predict girder end cumulative displacement, accounting for uncertainties inherent in the prediction process. Second, an anomaly detection algorithm utilizing a Mahalanobis distance–based approach is implemented to provide warnings to operations based on both measured and predicted data. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated using data collected from multiple loads and displacement responses of a suspension bridge. The analysis reveals that the GEV distribution is highly proficient in capturing the underlying pattern of the cumulative displacement indicator, enabling the establishment of an appropriate threshold. This method proves successful in identifying anomalies in critical components such as viscous dampers, enhancing predictive and preventive maintenance practices and contributing to the longevity and safety of bridge infrastructure. titulo: Towards an LLM-Powered Smart Home for Efficient and Safe Living Environment
titulo_norm: towards an llm powered smart home for efficient and safe living environment
resumo: The rapid advancements in Generative AI (GenAI), particularly the Large Language Models (LLMs) present transformative opportunities for enhancing smart home environments. This research investigates the integration of LLM agents as reasoning entities into smart homes, with a focus on optimizing energy efficiency, improving indoor living conditions, and addressing safety and security challenges. By leveraging their natural language processing and reasoning capabilities, LLM agents are used to analyze the data from sensors deployed across the smart home to identify usage patterns, detect anomalies, and generate actionable recommendations. The proposed framework demonstrates how LLM agents can optimize appliance settings, enable predictive maintenance, and mitigate vendor lock-in by providing a versatile and non-proprietary solution for intelligent home management. Key contributions of this research include the development of a platform for monitoring and maintaining energy efficiency and living comfort, as well as issuing structured recommendations aligned with standard living guidelines. The findings highlight the potential of LLMs in transforming smart home ecosystems, paving the way for more sustainable, efficient, and user-centric living environments.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Remaining Useful Life Prediction Methodologies With Health Indicator Dependence for Rotating Machinery: A Comprehensive Review
titulo_norm: remaining useful life prediction methodologies with health indicator dependence for rotating machinery a comprehensive review
resumo: Facilitated by artificial intelligence (AI) technologies such as deep learning (DL), predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as the most cost-effective maintenance approach for significantly enhancing the safety and availability of industrial equipment. Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rotating machinery (RM) is one of the core tasks of PdM, which can assist in maintenance decision-making and optimize asset allocation. Among them, the prognostic approach with health indicator (HI) as an intermediate bridge has attracted increasing attention due to its advantages in combining health condition monitoring (CM) and RUL prediction capabilities. Unfortunately, there has not been a comprehensive review to systematically analyze and summarize the recent advances in HI-dependent prognostic approaches. To fill this gap, this article comprehensively reviews the RUL prediction methods with HI dependence for RM to help researchers quickly outline the current research status and state-of-the-art methods. First, several run-to-failure datasets used to validate the performance of prognostic algorithms are briefly introduced. Second, three types of HI-based prognosis methods for RM, including similarity-based prognostic (SBP) methods, model and data-based statistical methods, and intelligent time series prediction (TSP) methods, are analyzed comprehensively. Finally, the current main challenges and prospects are presented to conclude this article. It is anticipated that the target audience of this article will be practitioners and researchers involved in the field of machinery PdM, providing them with the necessary basic knowledge and technical overview. © 1963-2012 IEEE.

titulo: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Internet of Things–Based Smart Grids and Power Systems
titulo_norm: machine learning deep learning and internet of things based smart grids and power systems
resumo: Machine learning, deep learning, and the Internet of Things (IoT) have revolutionized various domains, and the power sector is no exception. Smart grids and power systems have emerged as key areas of research and development, aiming to improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the electric grid. This chapter presents an overview of the integration of machine learning, deep learning, and IoT technologies in the context of smart grids and power systems. Firstly, we focus on machine learning techniques applied to smart grids, with discussing the utilization of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning algorithms for load forecasting, demand response, fault detection, and power system optimization. Then we explore the application of deep learning in smart grids. Deep learning algorithms, such as deep neural networks and convolutional neural networks, have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in image and signal processing tasks. They have been successfully employed for power system state estimation, fault diagnosis, renewable energy integration, and anomaly detection. The chapter highlights the advantages and challenges of using deep learning techniques in smart grids. Then in the last we move towards into the integration of IoT technologies in smart grids and power systems. The proliferation of IoT devices and sensors enables real-time monitoring, control, and communication within the grid infrastructure. This integration facilitates enhanced situational awareness, predictive maintenance, and demand-side management. Also, this chapter presents various IoT architectures, communication protocols, and security issues relevant to smart grids. © 2025 selection and editorial matter, Amit Kumar Tyagi and Shrikant Tiwari ; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Enhancing Pharmaceutical Batch Processes Monitoring with Predictive LSTM-Based Framework
titulo_norm: enhancing pharmaceutical batch processes monitoring with predictive lstm based framework
resumo: Monitoring industrial processes and understanding deviations is critical in ensuring product quality, process efficiency, and early detection of anomalies. Traditional methods for dimensionality reduction and anomaly detection, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) or Partial Least Squares (PLS), often struggle to capture the complex and dynamic nature of batch data. In this study, we propose a novel approach that combines an AutoEncoder (AE), based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers, with a rolling threshold for anomaly evaluation. Unlike conventional threshold methods that rely on global statistical parameters, the applied threshold leverages rolling median and rolling Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) to adaptively detect deviations, making it more resilient to outliers and distribution shifts. The LSTM-AE demonstrates superior performance in anomaly detection with respect to PCA and more recent model approaches, specifically for the reference dataset, obtained from a GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) production plant. Additionally, an LSTM regression model is employed to forecast future data points, which are then fed into the LSTM-AE to enable a predictive approach. This framework leverages the temporal dependencies captured by LSTM layers and reconstruction efficiency of the AE, facilitating a predictive anomaly detection in real-world applications.

titulo: Employ the Machine Learning Models for immediate Predictive Diagnostics: Anomaly detection of Industrial IoT
titulo_norm: employ the machine learning models for immediate predictive diagnostics anomaly detection of industrial iot
resumo: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has transformed plants and factories, facilitating real-time monitoring, automation, and informed decision-making. Nevertheless, in such complex data-rich environments, identification of the fault in a timely manner, detection of the anomaly, has become one of the most important challenges. Unresolved anomalies in IIoT systems can cause unscheduled maintenance, slippage in quality, or even catastrophic failure. The conventional rule-based models are not capable of accommodating the complicated dynamics and the non-linear dependencies that widely exist in industrial systems. In this study, the mixture machine learning (ML) models are applied for real-time predictive diagnostics and anomaly detection in the IIoT networks. System Overview The proposed system combines both supervised and unsupervised ML models getting the best of each of them such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Autoencoders, Isolation Forest, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. These models are learned and tested over massive time-series sensor data derived from IIoT ready industrial machines (e.g., pumps, motors, turbines, and conveyors). Method of feature extraction and the detection of temporal patterns are applied to find the abnormal behavior in the operational parameters: temperature, vibration, pressure and energy consumption. One of the key contributions in our study is that models could be deployed in real time and this is made possible by edge computation. By moving ML inference to the edge, the system provides quick response times even under bandwidth-constrained conditions. Alongside, long-term analytics trend forecasting and cross-facility model improvement is made possible via cloud-based aggregation. The combined alerting and strategic system along with hybrid structure allows operators to avoid catastrophic failures before they occur. Experiments on benchmark IIoT datasets show that the proposed models achieved excellent detection performance, e.g., more than 95% precision and recall for the temporal based model-LSTM. The ML-based approach is shown to vastly outperform conventional threshold-based detections in the presence of noisy, multivariate and asynchronous data. In addition, machine behavior evolves, and with it the ability to learn adapts diagnostic accuracy. This work underlines the disruptive nature of the ML for predictive maintenance and real-time industry diagnosis. Through a transition from reactive to proactive approaches, the developed framework minimizes downtime, lowers maintenance costs, and extends asset life. Incorporating smart diagnostics into the IIoT networks not only promotes operational efficiency, but also provides an infrastructural building block for the next-generation autonomous industrial systems that are data, intelligence, and connectivity enabled.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on Wind Turbine Multi-source Data-driven Predictive Diagnosis and Active Risk Early Warning Method for Safe Operation of the Wind Power System
titulo_norm: research on wind turbine multi source data driven predictive diagnosis and active risk early warning method for safe operation of the wind power system
resumo: The integration of large-scale wind power into the Energy Internet presents significant challenges for grid security due to sudden turbine component failures. This study presents a sequential LSTM-Transformer framework for early fault prediction of wind turbine gearbox and bearing components, utilizing high-frequency sensor data from the NREL dataset. The model captures both short-term temporal dynamics and long-range dependencies in multivariate vibration and temperature signals, enabling accurate, pre-fault predictions. Based on these forecasts, a predict-and-derate control strategy is developed to turn abrupt turbine shutdowns into managed, grid-friendly power adjustments. System-level simulations show that this approach smooths plant-level power output, reducing the Rate of Change of Frequency by 25% and lowering frequency nadir deviations by 18% during impending failures. By connecting component-level predictive maintenance with system-level control, the framework provides a validated pathway for enhancing the security, resilience, and flexibility of wind-integrated power systems, highlighting the potential of predictive digital twin-enabled wind farm operation. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo_norm: literature review on remote monitoring and control system for manufacturing equipment using iot
resumo: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies into manufacturing systems enables the remote monitoring and control of equipment, significantly enhancing operational efficiency, reducing downtime, and improving overall productivity. The paper presents a comprehensive solution for implementing IoT-based systems for real- time monitoring, fault detection, and predictive maintenance of manufacturing equipment. The proposed system utilizes sensors, cloud computing, and data analytics to collect and process operational data, providing insights that facilitate proactive decision-making and remote control of machinery. By enabling real-time visibility into equipment performance, the system not only minimizes unexpected failures but also optimizes resource utilization and extends the lifespan of machinery. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of IoT-enabled solutions in modern manufacturing environments, offering a pathway to smarter, more reliable production processes. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Interfacing Multi-modal AI with IoT: Unlocking New Frontiers
titulo_norm: interfacing multi modal ai with iot unlocking new frontiers
resumo: The combination of artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things has recently altered our way of perceiving and interacting with the world around us. We examine the possible relationships between multi-modal AI and Internet of Things technologies in the chapter “Interfacing Multi-modal AI with IoT” from the book Unlocking the Potential. We aim to find the good changes that can come from integrating these two systems. Understanding and analysing complicated real-life occurrences is made easier by multi-modal approaches within the framework of artificial intelligence. These approaches integrate the competency of numerous data modalities, such as text, images, and sensor data. With the combination of multi-modal AI and an abundance of data facilities powered by IoT devices, new possibilities for producing various forms of creativity and efficiency in various sectors emerge. An introduction to AI and the Internet of Things, outlining their fundamental concepts so that the reader may grasp their interconnection, is the first stop on this path. Our research also delves into the feasibility and efficacy of combining various forms of AI to address practical issues. Compatibility with the Internet of Things (IoT), real-time processing, data integration, and artificial intelligence (AI) are some of the problems that this book aims to solve. In addition, there is the investigation of how predictive analytics using automation that makes use of machine learning, AI, and data from the Internet of Things could revolutionise entire industries. All of this would be useful for learning about smart automation, predictive maintenance, and customer-specific services. This article presents reasons and examples to show how the health sector, manufacturing, transportation, and smart cities can all be transformed by integrating AI and the Internet of Things. When we think about the future of AI and the Internet of Things working together, some methodologies and trends are starting to emerge, such as quantum computing, federated learning, and edge computing. Furthermore, AS and personalised services backed by AI and IoT bring up ethical questions, as well as potential dangers and invasions of privacy. Combining multi-modal AI with the Internet of Things poses a disruptive danger, and this book provides a general view or outlook on that risk. In the coming age of the digital, this document could serve as a valuable resource for academics, technocrats, and legislators looking for a forum to debate and plan the further development of AI and the Internet of Things, as well as their potential applications as problem-solving tools and sources of economic benefit. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Digital Monitoring Systems Based on Artificial Intelligence for the Oil Industry
titulo_norm: digital monitoring systems based on artificial intelligence for the oil industry
resumo: Petroleum storage facilities are crucial to the global energy supply chain, functioning as intermediaries that ensure the safe storage and efficient transfer of hydrocarbons between production and consumption. Despite their critical role, these facilities face persistent challenges such as equipment failures, operational inefficiencies, and increasing safety controls and regulatory demands. Traditional systems like Distributed Control Systems (DCS) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), while effective for basic monitoring and specific tasks, lack the predictive and adaptive capabilities required for modern industrial demands. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative approach to addressing these challenges. Through real-time analytics, data processing, machine learning, and predictive maintenance, AI enhances operational reliability, safety, and cost-efficiency. This study explores the integration of AI into petroleum storage operations, detailing its methodology, outcomes, and implications for industrial modernization. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Synergising the data-driven digital twin: Predicting the remaining useful life of spacecraft battery modules
titulo_norm: synergising the data driven digital twin predicting the remaining useful life of spacecraft battery modules
resumo: The increasing global interest in the "new space race" and advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have driven rapid developments in space technology, particularly in satellite constellation management. One of the most critical challenges in this domain is where ageing satellite systems encounter difficulties, including but not limited to battery deterioration, heat complications, hardware obsolescence, fuel exhaustion, and mechanical malfunctions. As satellite constellations grow in complexity, traditional monitoring and management approaches are proving inadequate in ensuring optimal performance, longevity, and cost-effectiveness. To address these limitations, this research proposes a novel approach that integrates a Digital Twin with hybridised data-driven generative AI to create a synergised and autonomous Data-Driven Digital Twin and framework for satellite constellation management. This framework looks to enhance predictive maintenance, optimise operational efficiency, and extend mission lifespan through high-fidelity simulations powered by real-time data analytics. The methodology employed in this study follows a multi-phase approach with a focus on the various AI techniques and algorithms employed in the operation or maintenance of spacecraft batteries. Initially, a high-fidelity Digital Twin of the spacecraft battery module is design and configured using the electrical, thermal, and mechanical characteristics and properties to model its real-world behaviour. Several AI models are then trained with telemetry data from various space programs including a plethora of datasets obtained from simulation scenarios subject to user-defined, configurable, and controllable mechanical and navigational conditions including environmental factors. The Digital Twin battery model is continuously refined using hybrid machine learning techniques to enable predictive analysis and determination of remaining useful life (RUL). A key innovation of this approach is the integration of generative AI, which allows the system to simulate multiple operational scenarios, enabling proactive decision-making and strategic contingency planning ensuring the reliability and longevity of space missions. The predictive capabilities of the system enable early intervention before failures occur, reducing maintenance costs and minimising mission downtime. The conclusions drawn from this research highlights the transformative potential of integrating Digital Twin Technology with generative AI in space applications. The proposed data-driven digital twin (D3T) framework not only addresses current limitations in satellite constellation battery management and optimisation but also lays the groundwork for future advancements in autonomous space design and operations. The findings of this study emphasize the importance of incorporating a D3T model in the space mission loop, which facilitates parallel mission scenario modeling, revolutionizing satellite operations, ensuring more resilient, cost-effective and sustainable space missions in the era of rapid technological advancements. titulo: A composite network model for GIS insulation defect identification model considering the spatiotemporal PRPD pattern
titulo_norm: a composite network model for gis insulation defect identification model considering the spatiotemporal prpd pattern
resumo: This study introduces a novel hybrid deep learning model designed for precise identification of insulation anomalies in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) by thoroughly examining the spatial-temporal properties of phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) signatures. The developed framework combines the capabilities of convolutional neural networks (CNN) for spatial pattern recognition with long short-term memory networks (LSTM) for time-series data processing, facilitating efficient extraction and application of multi-dimensional attributes from PRPD patterns. Experimental validation demonstrates that the model achieves superior classification performance with an average accuracy of 93.33% in identifying partial discharge types associated with various insulation defects, representing a significant improvement over conventional analysis methods. The robust pattern recognition capability of this approach provides a reliable and efficient solution for GIS insulation diagnosis, with potential applications in predictive maintenance strategies. Furthermore, this research contributes to the advancement of intelligent power system monitoring by offering a scientifically validated methodology that enhances operational efficiency and ensures grid reliability, particularly in high-voltage transmission networks © 2025 SPIE.

titulo: Productive Intelligence: AI and Generative AI for Production Optimization and Predictive Maintenance in Oil and Gas Fields - Case Studies from the USA and India
titulo_norm: productive intelligence ai and generative ai for production optimization and predictive maintenance in oil and gas fields case studies from the usa and india
resumo: This paper describes real-world views of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (Gen AI) can be employed to enhance oil and gas well production optimization and predictive maintenance. We employed machine learning algorithms to predict and analyze day-to-day production, pressure, and equipment sensor readings. Generative models were used in parallel to simulate possible failure modes. From India and US case studies, we demonstrate how smart systems perceive and facilitate decision-making in order to improve production efficiency. Implementation of the methodology provided measurable improvement in performance. Downtime resulting from failures due to maintenance was predicted 15 to 20 percent more accurately and there was reduction in unplanned downtime by up to 18 percent. Overall, the findings show predictive analytics with generative simulation is a battle-tested, scalable solution that maximizes reliability and optimizes production for many operating conditions. They operated by taking in historical and real-time well data into machine learning models that were programmed to pick up on patterns that might otherwise be overlooked through traditional analysis. Gen AI, when married with digital twin-based modeling, allowed for predictive maintenance and failure scenario simulation, not only making operations smarter but also more responsive. Secondly, through the use of edge-computing models, the information produced could be retrieved nearly instantaneously by field personnel, enhancing response time to anomalies and maximizing daily operational tactics. This paper provides suggestions as to how contemporary AI methodologies can be adapted to the actual issues encountered in upstream oilfield activities, particularly in operations with sensor reliability problems, excessive gas-to-oil ratios, pump inefficiency, and challenging production conditions. Through three different case studies and proof of quantifiable performance improvement, we lay a compelling basis for incorporating AI and Gen AI into current digital transformation initiatives in the petroleum industry. titulo: Vibration-induced failures in industrial ventilation systems: A predictive maintenance approach
titulo_norm: vibration induced failures in industrial ventilation systems a predictive maintenance approach
resumo: Industrial ventilation systems are highly susceptible to vibration-induced failures, which can compromise operational efficiency and safety. This paper proposes a predictive maintenance (PdM) framework leveraging vibration-based condition monitoring, integrated with modern data analytics and IoT technologies. We analyze and compare conventional and advanced signal processing techniques, including Fast Fourier Transform, Wavelet, and Cepstrum analysis, as well as machine learning models for fault classification and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction. A simulated testbed based on benchmark datasets (e.g., PRONOSTIA) was used to evaluate model performance. Among various algorithms tested, Random Forest demonstrated the highest accuracy in fault detection. The study further incorporates edge computing, LoRaWAN, and wireless sensor networks (WSNs) into a scalable PdM system architecture. This approach enables real-time vibration monitoring and decision-making to preempt component-level failures. The results show the feasibility of an integrated, intelligent PdM solution for improving equipment lifespan and reducing unplanned downtime in industrial ventilation systems. © The Author(s) 2025

titulo: Intelligent Diagnostic System for Mechanical Fault Detection Using Deep Learning
titulo_norm: intelligent diagnostic system for mechanical fault detection using deep learning
resumo: Advanced diagnostic tools are essential for aerospace transportation systems and automotive industries and industrial manufacturing facilities since operational efficiency requirements and safety needs demand failure prediction tools. Systems that use traditional diagnostic methods depend on centralized architectures that show limitations regarding scalability while being unable to overcome subsystem failure events effectively. The research presents Gossip Neural Network (GNN) as a decentralized deep learning (DL) system which determines Remaining Useful Life (RUL) duration in distributed mechanical engine systems. The GNN combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long short-term Memory (LSTM) network layers to identify short-term sensor anomalies in addition to capturing long-term sensor degeneration patterns in sensor data. A gossip-based protocol allows the GNN to facilitate distributed engine subsystems which train a shared model together through peer-to-peer collaborations without needing central control. The assessment of the proposed framework using CMAPSS data proves its exceptional capability for RUL prediction alongside reliable accuracy and low error rates. The GNN demonstrated excellence in different datasets through R2 results between 92.43% and 94.57% and RMSE results within 12.77 to 12.87 which demonstrates its effectiveness in handling realistic operational environments. The GNN provides an encouraging solution for time-sensitive fault detection in distributed systems which facilitates efficient predictive maintenance across large engineering applications. ©2025 The Authors. titulo: Behavioral-Aware Early Destination Prediction Using LiDAR Point Clouds and Movement Trajectories
titulo_norm: behavioral aware early destination prediction using lidar point clouds and movement trajectories
resumo: Large-scale facility management increasingly relies on understanding human movement patterns, yet existing person re-identification (Re-ID) methods face challenges in tracking individuals across non-overlapping sensor regions. This paper presents a novel approach combining 3D LiDAR point cloud data with trajectory information to predict pedestrian destinations in early stages of movement. By predicting likely destinations, our method can significantly narrow down the search space for matching individuals between different sensor regions, thereby improving Re-ID accuracy. Our method leverages deep learning architectures - PointNet for processing point cloud data and LSTM for analyzing trajectory patterns - to capture both instantaneous behavioral characteristics and temporal movement patterns. Through experiments conducted with 33,110 trajectories in a university campus setting, our combined approach achieved 90.0% accuracy in predicting three destination categories (entrance, elevator/stairs, and meeting rooms), significantly out-performing single-modality approaches. The results demonstrate that early behavioral cues indeed carry significant predictive power for destination estimation. These findings have important implications for improving person tracking across distributed sensor networks and enabling proactive facility management systems.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Packaging Industry
titulo_norm: the impact of digital transformation on the packaging industry
resumo: Artificial intelligence is an advanced computing technology inspired by the mechanisms of human thinking and decision-making. AI technologies have transformed from theoretical concepts into practical implementations. They optimize the entire value chain in the packaging industry from design and production to quality control and life cycle management. These solutions provide a competitive advantage through increased operational efficiency, cost reduction, and quality parameters that cannot be achieved with conventional methods (Statista, 2024). The chapter focuses on the role of AI in the packaging value chain, from design and production to waste management, with a particular emphasis on its applications in predictive maintenance, quality control, process optimization, and compliance with new regulations. It covers AI-based innovations, including generative AI for creative packaging design, machine learning for production optimization, and computer vision for automated refuse sorting and defect detection. A few examples of how AI can support packaging companies in their marketing activities were also provided and the potential of AI integration to facilitate e-commerce and logistics was discussed. Moreover, the chapter includes an industrial case study of AI in thermoforming process modeling and operator assistance systems. © 2025 selection and editorial matter, Witold Abramowicz, Marek Kowalkiewicz and Krzysztof Węcel; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: AI-Driven Optimization of Integrated Solar PV and Smart Home Systems for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Predictive Maintenance
titulo_norm: ai driven optimization of integrated solar pv and smart home systems for enhanced energy efficiency and predictive maintenance
resumo: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) in residential energy management presents unprecedented opportunities for enhancing sustainability and efficiency in homes. Building on prior research indicating a 24% reduction in household energy consumption through smart home and solar photovoltaic (PV) integration, this study explores the AI driven synergy between Tesla Solar PV systems and Google Nest Smart Thermostats. Preliminary simulations demonstrate up to 35% additional energy savings, 20-30% extension in equipment lifespan, and 15% reduction in maintenance costs, underscoring the potential for AI-driven optimization in real-time energy flow, predictive maintenance, and reduced grid dependency. titulo: CAPTAIN: A Testbed for Co-Simulation of Scalable Serverless Computing Environments for AIoT Enabled Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0
titulo_norm: captain a testbed for co simulation of scalable serverless computing environments for aiot enabled predictive maintenance in industry 4 0
resumo: The massive amounts of data generated by the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) require considerable processing power, which increases carbon emissions and energy usage, and we need sustainable solutions to enable flexible manufacturing. Serverless computing shows potential for meeting this requirement by scaling idle containers to zero energy-efficiency and cost, but this will lead to a cold start delay. Most solutions rely on idle containers, which necessitates dynamic request time forecasting and container execution monitoring. Furthermore, Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) can provide autonomous and sustainable solutions by combining IIoT with artificial intelligence (AI) to solve this problem. Therefore, we develop a new testbed, CAPTAIN, to facilitate AI-based co-simulation of scalable and flexible serverless computing in IIoT environments. The AI module in the CAPTAIN framework employs random forest (RF) and light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM) models to optimize cold start frequency and prevent cold starts based on their prediction results. The proxy module additionally monitors the client-server network and constantly updates the AI module training dataset via a message queue. Finally, we evaluated the proxy module’s performance using a predictive maintenance-based real-world IIoT application and the AI module’s performance in a realistic serverless environment using a Microsoft Azure dataset. The AI module of the CAPTAIN outperforms baselines in terms of cold start frequency, computational time with 0.5 ms, energy consumption with 1161.0 joules, and CO2 emissions with 32.25e-05 gCO2. The CAPTAIN testbed provides a co-simulation of sustainable and scalable serverless computing environments for AIoT-enabled predictive maintenance in Industry 4.0. © 2014 IEEE.

titulo: Leveraging IoT, Big Data and AI Capabilities for Technological Regenerative Innovation in Commercial and Industrial Energy Management
titulo_norm: leveraging iot big data and ai capabilities for technological regenerative innovation in commercial and industrial energy management
resumo: Traditional energy management systems in the commercial and industrial (C&I) built environment rely on reactive maintenance and fixed operational parameters, leading to sub-optimal energy efficiency and increased operational costs. This paper presents a comprehensive data driven framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, Big Data analytics platforms, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to transform energy management from reactive to predictive framework. The proposed technological regenerative innovation(TRI) framework employs real time IoT enabled condition monitoring to collect granular data related to mostly energy consumption, which is processed through machine learning algorithms or SHAP (SHapley Additive Explanations) analysis providing interpretable insights into energy consumption patterns and decision making strategies as compared to conventional statistical analysis, to ensure transparency and stakeholder trust. Two case studies show the practicality of the TRI framework's effectiveness: (i) a commercial chiller system and (ii) an industrial chiller facility in which hourly data was considered which showed predictive accuracy with ML models. The industrial case study presented critical operational parameters through SHAP analysis, identifying key parameters driving primary energy consumption. A scalable TRI framework, applicable for autonomous energy systems, increases improvement in predictive and provides actionable XAI insights enabling targeted energy analysis for system efficiency and sustainability. Through practical implementation, proposed TRI framework provides energy managers with transparent, AI-driven tools that shift energy management from reactive maintenance to predictive optimization, delivering actionable insights through SHAP analysis and reliable forecasting capabilities.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Next-Generation Power Systems: A 5G-Enabled Framework for Grid Optimization and Resilience
titulo_norm: ai driven predictive maintenance for next generation power systems a 5g enabled framework for grid optimization and resilience
resumo: In this work, the potential of AI-driven approaches for predictive maintenance in next-generation power system planning has been explored, drawing parallels with adaptive machine learning strategies applied in 5G network slicing. Adaptive methods that learn and evolve over time have been compared with traditional, static techniques in terms of their effectiveness in enhancing power grid performance under dynamic environmental and operational conditions. Through experiments that mimic real-world conditions, advanced tools like multi-line graphs, 3D charts, heatmaps, and maps showing geographic data have been used to show how different models handle problems and help make the power grid more reliable. The results show that using smart AI strategies works much better than old methods. These strategies can adjust to changes outside the system, use resources more efficiently, and keep the system stable. The findings also show that machine learning plays a big role in modern power systems, especially in predicting faults, guessing how much electricity will be needed, and finding unusual problems. Using smart solutions can make power grids more efficient, stronger, and better for the environment. However, there are still major challenges when trying to use AI widely. These challenges show the need for better ability to adjust in real time and for AI decisions to be easier to understand. Overall, the study gives a clear plan for using smart AI in future power systems, offering useful advice for building smarter grids and dealing with current issues. The knowledge from this study helps connect new ideas with real-life use in important energy systems. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Evolutionary method of digital twin model for building physics mechanism
titulo_norm: evolutionary method of digital twin model for building physics mechanism
resumo: Building digital twin (BDT) realizes real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization control of the building system through the synchronization between the real world and the virtual platform, and improves the efficiency of building operation and maintenance. However, the changes in physical laws caused by the decline and aging of buildings make it difficult for the BDT models to depict the dynamic evolution mechanism of buildings and improve decision-making, which brings great challenges to the prediction and maintenance of buildings. To this end, an evolutionary method of digital twin model for building physics mechanisms is proposed, which integrates the internet of things (IoT), building information physical model (BIPM), and machine learning algorithms to build a self-evolution framework of digital twins for building physics mechanism, and supports high-precision modeling of BDTs. The advanced prediction (AP) model and autonomous decision-making (ADM) model for building physics mechanisms with self-evolution capability are designed, which support the autonomous correction of model parameters and the dynamic updating of the model driven by real-time data, and the ability to learn optimal control actions through interactive trial and error with the environment. The experimental results based on the settlement prediction and control case of underground engineering show that this evolutionary method can dynamically simulate the future evolution trend of the settlement law of underground engineering, and adjust the physical parameters to the ideal range to guide the evolution of underground engineering in a better direction. Compared with the existing methods, it has better prediction accuracy, interpretability, and generalization performance. © 2024 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

titulo: Graph-Based Visualization and Fault Diagnosis in Large-Scale Industrial Sensor Networks Using KNN-Constructed Graph Neural Networks(GNN)-A Approach Synthetic Dataset
titulo_norm: graph based visualization and fault diagnosis in large scale industrial sensor networks using knn constructed graph neural networks gnn a approach synthetic dataset
resumo: In this study, we present a scalable method for modeling and visualizing large-scale industrial sensor networks using Graph Neural Network (GNN) principles. By applying the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm to high-dimensional sensor data-including vibration, temperature, humidity, pressure, voltage, and current-we construct a featuresimilarity graph of 1 0, 0 0 0 nodes, where each node represents an individual sensor. A 2D structure is visualized and is achieved using NetworkX with a spring layout for nodes and edges data. The graph edges encode proximity in feature space and are converted into formats compatible with PyTorch Geometric, facilitating GNN-based analysis. Nodes are color-coded based on operational status: green for normal and red for faulty. Approximately 40,000 edges reveal both local and global internode relationships. This graph structure representation allows for intuitive inspection of anomaly clusters and reveals spatial fault patterns. The proposed approach supports intelligent monitoring and decision-making in dealing with complex networks of data. The framework also incorporates exception handling of robustness in network data with graph construction. The potential applications are in structural health monitoring, predictive maintenance, and cyber-physical system optimization. The paper emphasizes the effectiveness of graphbased modeling in identifying abnormal behavior for different sensor locations and networks and validating GNN models. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models for Sustainable and Intelligent Transportation Systems in the Electric Vehicle Era

resumo: Urban ecosystems in the midst of digital transformation utilize technologies like Internet of Things (IoT), big data, and artificial intelligence (AI) to elevate citizens’ well-being and champion sustainable development. Notably, LLMs such as GPT-3 or GPT-4, crafted by OpenAI, and Google’s AI tools like Gemini and Bard, stand as pivotal components, holding immense potential to revolutionize EVs in smart city initiatives. Generative AI and LLM integration prove influential in optimizing EV functionalities, enhancing security, and fortifying data privacy. This chapter delves into battery technology, battery capacities, energy storage, charging infrastructure optimization, autonomous driving, educational outreach, energy management, and predictive maintenance. In particular, LLMs address EV challenges by optimizing routes, speeds, and behaviors, reducing energy usage and emissions. They facilitate the smart integration of EVs and renewable energy sources, managing charging schedules based on availability and grid demands. Additionally, LLMs contribute to public education on EV benefits, environmental impact, cost savings, and sustainable transportation promotion. The chapter explores synergies between LLMs and EVs, focusing on potential applications and challenges, propelling progress in ITSs. Similarly, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and their potential applications in the era of the EV represent a promising frontier in this landscape, offering enhanced capabilities to interpret and generate multimodal data, further enriching the EV ecosystem. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Predictive Maintenance powered by Artificial Intelligence using Models of Bayesian Inference in Manufacturing
titulo_norm: predictive maintenance powered by artificial intelligence using models of bayesian inference in manufacturing
resumo: Predictive maintenance powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming manufacturing by enabling early detection of potential equipment failures, reducing downtime, and optimizing operational efficiency. Traditional maintenance approaches, such as scheduled or reactive maintenance, often fail to prevent unexpected breakdowns, leading to increased costs and production losses. To address these challenges, we propose a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN)-based framework for failure prediction, leveraging Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty in predictions. Unlike conventional deep learning models, BNNs integrate probabilistic reasoning, allowing for more reliable decision-making by estimating confidence levels in failure predictions. This enhances robustness, particularly in cases of limited or noisy data. The proposed method continuously analyzes sensor data from manufacturing equipment, updating failure probability distributions in real time. By doing so, it facilitates proactive maintenance scheduling, minimizing disruptions and optimizing resource utilization. Experimental results demonstrate that our BNN-based approach outperforms traditional machine learning models in predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation. The findings indicate improved failure detection rates, reduced false positives, and enhanced reliability in maintenance planning, ultimately leading to cost savings and increased manufacturing efficiency.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Role of Generative AI in Data Engineering to Build Scalable Models in Cloud Technology
titulo_norm: role of generative ai in data engineering to build scalable models in cloud technology
resumo: The importance of data engineering has been highlighted by the quick development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) models, especially as more businesses look to cloud-based platforms for adaptable and scalable data management solutions. Building and maintaining the infrastructure required to gather, process, store, and convert data from multiple sources-including sensors-is the core goal of data engineering. An important component of data engineering is the examination of sensor data. This study examines the potential application of machine learning (ML) methods for predictive maintenance (PdM) in horizontal and vertical CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machining centers. The study focusses on scalable applications for evaluating sensor data from machine components, such as oil density sensors, temperature, pressure, vibration, and gas content detection. Several Gen AI driven machines learning models, including LightGBM, XGBoost, and AdaBoost, are trained and tested using a dataset of sensor readings gathered over a week. Accuracy ratings and the precision/recall or F1 score are used to evaluate the model's performance. Therefore, this study demonstrates that machine learning models can use sensor data to generate extremely accurate predictions, thereby meeting the requirement for a truly proactive maintenance approach that can improve overall productivity, decrease downtime, and increase resource use efficiency in manufacturing industries. The results show that predictive maintenance techniques have advanced, creating chances to create industry-forward plans. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Real-time damage detection and classification in wind turbine gearboxes using Ferderated learning
titulo_norm: real time damage detection and classification in wind turbine gearboxes using ferderated learning
resumo: Gearbox failures are a primary cause of wind turbine downtime, and while vibration-based monitoring is effective, centralising sensitive operational data for model training raises significant privacy and security concerns. This work proposes a federated learning (FL) framework to overcome this limitation, enabling collaborative training of a fault diagnosis model without the need to share raw vibration data from individual turbines. The selection of FL is critically justified by its unique ability to address data privacy mandates while leveraging distributed on-site data, a capability centralised learning models lack. Our methodology involves preprocessing sensor data, identifying in- formative sensors via outlier detection and ranking, and training a global neural network model across multiple client turbines using the Flower framework. The principal contribution of this paper is the development and comprehensive evaluation of an FL system under realistic, non-IID data distributions, demonstrating that such a privacy-preserving approach does not compromise diagnostic performance. Experimental findings demonstrate that the FL model successfully achieved stable convergence and high classification accuracy (92% to 99%) in distinguishing healthy operations from seven specific fault types. This work establishes FL as a robust alternative to conventional methods for building accurate, privacy-preserving predictive maintenance systems in the wind energy sector, offering a practical path to industry-wide collaboration without compromising data sovereignty. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Reliable Roadside Assistance and Fast Solutions for Emergency Breakdown States by EF-YOLOv8m
titulo_norm: reliable roadside assistance and fast solutions for emergency breakdown states by ef yolov8m
resumo: In the technological development era and fast-paced world, Artificial Intelligence techniques and Computer Vision algorithms are transfiguring the automotive industrial services, especially in reliable roadside assistance and emergency services for vehicle breakdowns. Significant AI-oriented algorithms including predictive maintenance, route optimization, resource allocation, and reinforcement learning techniques are used to address crucial problems like optimized resource distribution, rapid response, and proactive fault detection. This article incorporates AI-oriented algorithms for enhancing the accuracy, responsiveness, and efficiency of reliable roadside assistance and fast solutions for emergency breakdown states using the EF-YOLOv8m (Efficient - You Only Look Once version 8) algorithm. This proposed algorithm facilitates the visual prediction of breakdown situations and provides a fast solution for real-time prediction, analysis, and response in emergencies. The deployment of the EF - YOLOv8m algorithm leads to accurate prediction of vehicle breakdown situations, estimates road conditions, and detects critical faults to ensure the optimization of resource allocation and fast decision-making. Using its greater speed, accuracy, and lightweight model architecture, EE-YOLOv8 may process real-time image/video inputs and sensor data from vehicle-attached cameras, IoT devices, and surveillance drones in real time. Based on performance metrics such as confidence scores, detection accuracy, and frames per second (FPS), this model is used to analyse the reliability of EF-YOLOv8m in dynamic roadside environments. Additionally, the incorporation of AI -oriented and predictive maintenance algorithms improves the effectiveness of dispatch functions, reducing delay and guaranteeing timely assistance. Experimental results show the potential of YOLOv8m to transfigure the services of roadside assistance and provide an ascendable, high-performance solution that can address the difficulties of emergency breakdown situations with reliability and precision.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Supplier selection for global service providers: a decision support system
titulo_norm: supplier selection for global service providers a decision support system
resumo: In this paper, we develop a decision support system (DSS) aimed at solving a real-world supplier selection problem (SSP) for a global service provider (GSP) operating in the facility management (FM) industry. The GSP provides its customers with FM services, which are subcontracted to external suppliers selected on the basis of multiple criteria, like economic soundness, quality of service, capacity, and closeness. The SSP is formulated as a multi-objective generalized assignment problem, where the quality and the closeness of the selected suppliers are maximized, whereas a penalty produced by overcapacity assignments is minimized. The quality of each supplier is computed by applying a weighted sum method, resulting from a multi-criteria decision analysis in which the criteria weights are determined through an Analytic Hierarchy Process. The DSS is developed using a modular architecture with a relational database, a supplier evaluator, and a simulator, as well as an additional user-friendly interface. The simulator relies on a rolling horizon algorithm and three alternative configurations to assign contracts to suppliers. titulo: Beam shaping, process monitoring and AI join forces for the benefit of e-mobility
titulo_norm: beam shaping process monitoring and ai join forces for the benefit of e mobility
resumo: Photonic production chains represent a transformative approach to manufacturing, leveraging the unique properties lasers for material processing. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into these processes further enhances efficiency and adaptability, paving the way for more intricate designs and optimized production outcomes. This became even clearer in the context of battery and e-mobility applications. AI-driven methods in photonic production chains enable real-time monitoring, adaptive control, and predictive maintenance of laser systems. By analyzing vast amounts of data from the manufacturing process, AI can dynamically adjust laser parameters such as power, pulse duration, and beam shape, ensuring optimal performance and reducing material waste. Machine learning algorithms also facilitate defect detection and quality assurance, making the process more reliable and less dependent on manual intervention. Shaped light, a technique involving the manipulation of laser beam profiles, plays a critical role in enhancing the precision and versatility of laser material processing. By customizing the intensity distribution of the laser beam, shaped light allows for more controlled energy deposition, enabling the processing of a wide range of materials with varying properties. This capability is particularly useful in applications such as micro-machining, additive manufacturing, and surface texturing, where precision is paramount. The combination of AI methods and shaped light in photonic production chains leads to a highly adaptable and intelligent manufacturing system. This integration not only improves the accuracy and speed of production but also opens new possibilities for creating advanced materials and components. © 2025 SPIE.

titulo: Technology Trends and Digital Transformation in Construction
titulo_norm: technology trends and digital transformation in construction
resumo: This chapter provides an in-depth exploration of technology trends and the ongoing digital transformation within the construction industry. It examines the latest advancements in construction technology, including building information modeling (BIM), Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR), robotics, and blockchain. Through theoretical frameworks and practical examples, readers gain insights into the impact of these technologies on various aspects of construction project management, such as design, planning, execution, quality control, and facility management. The chapter explores the benefits of digital transformation, including improved productivity, enhanced safety, better quality control, and increased sustainability, as well as the challenges associated with adopting digital tools and technologies, such as resistance to change, workforce skill gaps, and data security concerns. Additionally, it discusses strategies for successful implementation, including best practices for integrating digital tools into workflows, change management approaches, collaboration with technology providers, and human-centered design principles. By understanding the evolving landscape of technology in construction, professionals can harness innovative solutions to address industry challenges and drive positive change in project delivery processes. The chapter concludes with a look at future trends, emphasizing the need for continuous adaptation and innovation in an increasingly digitalized construction sector. © 2025 Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd.

titulo: A survey on predictive maintenance for manufacturing using data mining techniques
titulo_norm: a survey on predictive maintenance for manufacturing using data mining techniques
resumo: This paper delves into the significance of predictive maintenance, a technique leveraging intelligent sensors for efficient data collection and evaluation to prevent problems and accidents. A data-focused predictive maintenance system has been established for manufacturing production lines, facilitating the identification of potential issues before they occur. Machine learning plays a pivotal role in predicting the precise moment when industrial equipment requires repair, ensuring quick problem-solving and adaptive decisionmaking. The paper’s goal is to conduct a comprehensive literature analysis of Data Mining and Machine Learning methods tailored for predictive maintenance, emphasizing those currently under examination in this domain, and showcasing the practical applications of the most advanced Machine Learning techniques. This review provides a unique and in-depth exploration of the evolving landscape of Data Mining and Machine Learning methods within the context of predictive maintenance in manufacturing. Beyond a mere survey, it showcases the potential of cutting-edge Machine Learning methodologies to revolutionize predictive maintenance practices.
