resumo: Effective anomaly management is essential for ensuring the reliability and performance of multi-robot systems operating in complex indoor environments. Increasing deployment of robots across logistics, manufacturing, and facility management requires capabilities to detect, classify, and respond to abnormal operational conditions. This paper proposes a web-based monitoring and notification framework designed to detect and visualize key anomalies during mobile robot operations, built on the Robotics Middleware Framework (RMF). The proposed system identifies and classifies anomalies by analyzing both robot-specific data and inter-robot behavior dynamics. Detected anomalies are shared in real time via a centralized dashboard, enabling both operators and system components to perceive and respond to issues collaboratively. The system consists of anomaly definition rules, data-driven detection logic, and a visualization interface implemented on the web. Validation in an RMF-based simulation environment demonstrates improved visibility into abnormal conditions and enhanced responsiveness in robot operations. © 2025 ICROS.

By integrating IoT data streams with an LSTM-based machine learning (ML) module, the framework provides actionable insights for proactive decision-making, helping to streamline facility management (FM) workflows and enhance collaboration among stakeholders. titulo: Predictive Finance Maintenance of Textile Machinery using Machine Learning Models
titulo_norm: predictive finance maintenance of textile machinery using machine learning models
resumo: The textile industry is supported by the long-term stability of the machinery, the breakdown of which leads to considerable uncontrolled loss of time, the reorganization of production processes, and the cost of maintenance. To overcome this problem, machine learning models have been employed together with predictive maintenance to predict failures and optimize maintenance schedules. The proposed model will be based on the works of the trainers of Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Gradient Boosting using sensor and financial cost data, which will be collected throughout the textile machine operation. Based on the experimental results, it can be seen that the performance of the Random Forest model has been demonstrated to be better than that of the other models tested, and with six times more data, the accuracy of the model was 96.8%, the precision was 95.7%, and the recall was 96.4%. A comparative analysis with other methods reveals that reliability increases by approximately 4-6% and the maintenance cost is reduced by 12%. The proposed method will enable improved decision-making in maintenance planning, lead to a reduction in unplanned breakdowns, and facilitate the allocation of improved resources. titulo: Empirical Quantification and Prediction of Building Component Lifespans with Graph Neural Networks
titulo_norm: empirical quantification and prediction of building component lifespans with graph neural networks
resumo: Extending the service life of existing buildings and their components is essential for slowing resource loops in circular construction. While overall building lifespans are relatively well understood, the actual service lives of individual components remain underexplored due to limited empirical data. This study addresses this gap by analyzing and modeling building component lifespans using real-world damage investigation records and condition assessments from Swedish buildings. Descriptive statistics reveal a wide range of lifespans across six major component categories, highlighting materials linked to damage from poorly designed construction details as a critical factor. Additionally, most residential components have markedly shorter lifespans-about 25-30 years-compared to non-residential ones. To predict component service lifespans, we configure building envelope deterioration factors as a generic acyclic graph and employ Graph Neural Networks for node-level regression. Among the tested models, Graph Convolutional Network achieved the highest performance (R2 = 0.83), outperforming GraphSAGE and Graph Attention Network due to its effective uniform aggregation across neighboring nodes. Our findings provide a high-granular, data-driven approach to estimating component lifespans, which can enhance predictive maintenance strategies and optimize the reuse potential of reclaimed materials in their next lifecycles. © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

resumo: This paper addresses the challenge of assessing workplace health through building maintenance requests’data, particularly focusing on the impact of maintenance conditions on workers' satisfaction, well-being and possible stress levels. A data-driven methodology based on CMMS (Computer Management Maintenance Systems) is proposed, utilizing indexes to measure both the quantity and perceived quality of maintenance interventions. Sentiment and emotion analysis, along with lexical diversity indices, are applied to capture the perceptions of end-users and technical staff. The methodology successfully identifies maintenance issues in buildings and highlights differences in perception between workers' typologies. The results provide valuable insights for facility managers and organizations, enabling better-informed decisions on maintenance priorities based on both objective data and workers' feedback. This approach paves the way for future research integrating qualitative and quantitative data in facility management, with the potential to enhance decision-making and improve workplace health. © 2025 The author(s).

titulo: Texture-Based Classification Techniques for Sports Surface and Equipment Analysis Using Deep Learning
titulo_norm: texture based classification techniques for sports surface and equipment analysis using deep learning
resumo: This study explores the application of advanced texture-based classification techniques employing deep learning (DL) architectures for analyzing sports surfaces and equipment. Recognizing that surface textures and material properties play a crucial role in sports performance, safety, and maintenance, the research evaluates the effectiveness of various deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and vision transformers, in accurately identifying and categorizing surface materials and equipment textures. Using a curated dataset of surface and material images, the models' performance was compared against traditional machine learning (ML) approaches reliant on hand-engineered features. The results demonstrate the superiority of deep learning models, with the Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) achieving a peak accuracy of 98%, significantly outperforming classical methods which reached a maximum of 72% accuracy. This research provides a robust framework for automated quality control and predictive maintenance in sports facility management, showcasing a practical application of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) in automation that enhances safety and operational efficiency. Furthermore, the study discusses practical considerations such as computational efficiency, model interpretability, and deployment challenges, paving the way for real-world implementation of AI-driven surface and equipment analysis in sports technology. © 2025 IEEE.

resumo: The Internet of Things (IoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are pacesetters to advance intelligent and connected environments, and their ubiquitous adoption will bring radical impact to critical domains including smart cities, healthcare, and autonomous systems. The transformative impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the CPS-IoT ecosystems is investigated in this paper. With AI, real time decision making, predictive maintenance, and even system optimisation is possible - all possible while solving the problem of scalability, latency, adaptability in highly dynamic environments. This paper provides unique insights into the convergence of AI, CPSs and IoT by presenting novel technologies like edge computing, digital twins, and AI-based cybersecurity. Overall, these advances illustrate the potential of AI-driven CPSs to realize next generation smarter, safer and more efficient systems. Finally, the paper also discusses critical challenges, primarily related to data privacy, ethical considerations as well as interoperability and suggests possible ways to overcome these barriers. The main findings underscore AI's central importance to next generation CPS-IoT systems and suggest a pathway for building secure, adaptive, and sustainable infrastructures. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Measuring Resilience from Cascading Transfer Learning in Manufacturing Systems
titulo_norm: measuring resilience from cascading transfer learning in manufacturing systems
resumo: Machine learning (ML) models are increasingly embedded in production systems to enable predictive maintenance, quality control, and adaptive decision-making. While the datadriven nature of ML affords opportunities for resilience through retraining and transfer learning, methods for measuring the resilience of production systems with ML components remain underdeveloped. Existing ML resilience research often conflates robustness and resilience, and focuses narrowly on model-level performance metrics without connecting them to system-level outcomes. In this paper, we contribute a method for measuring resilience in production systems with ML components by constructing resilience curves that relate throughput to time across stages of model degradation and recovery. Building on prior work that links false positive rates in machine condition classifiers to downtime rates, we extend the analysis to show how transfer learning mechanisms influence the dynamic response of production systems. Using simulation results, we demonstrate how resilience metrics such as degradation rate, recovery rate, and time to recovery can be derived from throughput curves, and how sampling rates impact resilience outcomes. This approach bridges ML resilience and production system resilience, providing a foundation for integrated system design and evaluation. © 2025 IEEE.

resumo: This study focuses on the criticality of failure detection and condition-based maintenance (CBM) within the semiconductor industry, employing Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) systems and Machine Learning (ML) techniques for equipment log analysis to anticipate equipment conditions and timely maintenance. Initiatives emphasize the cultivation of data engineering experts, enhancing depth in data analytics and equipment monitoring. Moreover, the imperative to advance the field lies in the development of innovative sensor technologies, a task that necessitates close collaboration with equipment manufacturers. This strategic partnership is indispensable for augmenting the precision and breadth of data acquisition. It ultimately enables more sophisticated analytics, thereby facilitating the creation of advanced predictive failure models through enhanced data capture and analysis. This paper illustrates the semiconductor sector's competitive adoption of diverse strategies and technologies for maintenance innovation, aiming to bolster industry productivity, equipment reliability, and sustainability. titulo: COTP: Coplanning and Coexecuting AIGC Agent Native Product for Predictive Maintenance and Operational Optimisation of Cross Border Transition Pipelines
titulo_norm: cotp coplanning and coexecuting aigc agent native product for predictive maintenance and operational optimisation of cross border transition pipelines
resumo: The Cross-border long-distance gas pipeline (CLGP) is a key energy corridor for China, ensuring energy supply and optimising consumption. With improved operational precision, allied decision-making is needed for pipeline health and gas transmission planning, integrating operational status, macroeconomic factors, geopolitics, and market forecasts. This manuscript introduces pipeline decision support system product (COTP), a generative AI agent based decision support system, enabling natural language interaction, flow transmitting simulation, and predictive maintenance for CLGP. COTP leverages multi-role generative agent technology to address gas transmission volume, pipeline operation, maintenance strategy decisions in CLGP. It operates through an autonomous loop of issue identification, code generation and work execution, output ranking, insight generation, and refinement. COTP relies entirely on natural language interaction, enabling users to initiate decision-making via prompt engineering, by agents outputting gas transmission plans, and with respect to corresponding maintenance suggestions if necessary. To enhance prediction and decision-making accuracy, COTP supports collaborative optimisation using voting and game theory achieved by multiple agents. It integrates multi-source heterogeneous data from internal and external sources via large models' online query capabilities, facilitating task breakdown and execution through deep thinking. A human-in-the-loop (HIL) design allows real-time user interaction during agent thinking and execution, ensuring decision-making aligns with user intent. COTP's steerability, user experience, prediction accuracy, and interpretability were validated using actual pipeline operating data, including historical CLGP scheduling reports, SCADA/PPS monitoring data, inventory levels, weather conditions, and commodity price fluctuations. 12 pipeline scheduling employers (6 online, 6 offline; 6 males, 6 females) evaluated COTP by comparing it with baseline methods-direct prompt-based generative AI and optimising computation for gas transmission decisions and maintenance strategies. Volunteers provided subjective and objective ratings on a 0-5 scale (strongly disagree to completely agree) to assess steerability, user experience, problem-solving, and refinements in terms of comparative studies over the task executed by COTP and baseline, respectively. All volunteers acknowledged COTP's steerability and user experiences, favouring its HIL, step-in interaction design over the baseline for enhanced stability. COTP demonstrated superior autonomous problem detection and robustness. Most volunteers agreed COTP enabled effective data-driven predictions and insights, while the baseline exhibited inconsistent performance and unreliable refinement ability. Although code generation category remain similar, it remained few existent since the baseline's overall process lacked significance. This findings verified that through innovative product interaction design, COTP has achieved fully natural language prompt driven co-planning, co-executing and decision-making processes, enabling autonomous execution and refinement. It provided simpler and efficient user-experience for complex decision-making in CLGP transition operation. COTP has distilled a more agile product interaction, leveraging rapid iteration capabilities of generative AI. By adapting to different target scenarios, it has potential to achieve rapid applications in equipment management, preventive maintenance, and spare parts strategy formulation across other domains. Compared to baseline, COTP's autonomous refinement capabilities offer more reasonable, feasible, and scientifically grounded solutions for complex decision-making challenges. titulo: Statistical Process Control Applied to Monitoring of Cable Networks
titulo_norm: statistical process control applied to monitoring of cable networks
resumo: Statistical Process Control and control charts, long-established quality control methodologies in manufacturing and process industries, have recently emerged as powerful tools for monitoring and optimizing cable networks. Building upon decades of successful implementations in sectors ranging from semiconductor fabrication to pharmaceutical production, this paper presents an adaptation of those methodologies to cable network monitoring. Traditional network monitoring approaches relied on expert-informed global thresholds for detection of out-of-control events, limiting the ability to detect device-specific anomalies and performance degradation. Our implementation leverages individualized control charts for subscriber gateways, enabling dynamic threshold computation based on historical device behavior rather than system-wide metrics. By analyzing device-specific patterns and variations, the methodology demonstrates improved anomaly detection precision compared to global threshold approaches. Furthermore, the refined granularity of device-level control charts provides higher quality training data for backend machine learning algorithms, reducing false positives and enhancing predictive maintenance capabilities. This approach demonstrates significant potential for improving network reliability and maintenance efficiency in next-generation cable networks through data-driven, device-specific monitoring strategies. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: IoT- Enabled Manufacturing System with Freertos Using CAN Protocol for Predictive Maintenance
titulo_norm: iot enabled manufacturing system with freertos using can protocol for predictive maintenance
resumo: This paper presents an intelligent industrial automation system for predictive maintenance. This system combines real-time embedded control and cloud-based analytics to improve efficiency and availability. The real-time embedded components of the system use ESP32 microcontrollers to acquire data from sensors (temperature, voltage, current, and vibration) to monitor the health of a machine in real-time. The sensor signals from Sensor node are sent to the Central node transmitted via the CAN protocol using MCP2515 transceivers. The Central node implements a real-time operating system, FreeRTOS, allowing tasks to run concurrently to facilitate an efficient embedded processing. Sensor data is transmitted to the Azure IoT Hub using the MQTT protocol, which is lightweight for real-time transmission. A logistic regression model was trained in the Azure Machine Learning environment, and the algorithm was instantiated to perform binary classification on the incoming sensor data using supervised learning to predict the maintenance requirements and then predictive results are stored in a scalable SQL Server database for further analysis. Finally, the system integrates with Power BI to visualize both raw sensor data and predictive outputs through an interactive dashboard. The predictive capability helps in visualizing real-time machine health, current sensor data, and anticipated maintenance. The implemented system reliably handles sensor data, performs real-time embedded data processing, demonstrates high accuracy of predictive analytics and the cloud-based machine learning in a scalable solution for predictive maintenance in modern industry.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Predictive Maintenance Based on Deep Learning: Early Identification of Failures in Heavy Machinery Components
titulo_norm: predictive maintenance based on deep learning early identification of failures in heavy machinery components
resumo: Deep learning-based predictive maintenance is a key strategy in industry to prevent unexpected failures, reduce downtime, and improve operational safety. This study presents an advanced approach for early fault detection in heavy machinery components using image analysis, focusing on four critical defect types: hose wear, piston failure, corrosion, and moisture. To this end, three state-of-the-art object detection models were implemented and compared: YOLOv11, RT-DETR, and YOLO-World. The dataset consists of images captured in real-life industrial environments exhibiting variations in lighting, texture, and material degradation. A manual preprocessing and annotation process was applied to improve training quality. Model performance was evaluated using key metrics such as the precision-recall (PR) curve and the confusion matrix to determine the most efficient technique for real-time fault detection. Experimental results show that YOLOv11 achieves the highest overall accuracy, with an mAP@0.5 of 83.8%, followed by YOLO-World at 82.4% and RT-DETR at 80.3%. In terms of efficiency, YOLO-World offers a balance between accuracy and detection speed, while RT-DETR shows stable performance but lower accuracy for certain defect types. These findings confirm that deep learning-based detection models enable the rapid and accurate identification of industrial defects, facilitating the implementation of predictive maintenance strategies. © (2025), (Science and Information Organization). titulo: A FRAMEWORK FOR REDUCING O&M COSTS AT OFFSHORE WIND FARMS
titulo_norm: a framework for reducing o m costs at offshore wind farms
resumo: Offshore wind farm operations and maintenance costs are estimated at approximately 30% of its lifetime costs, reducing this share is key for facilitating further deployment of offshore wind developments. This paper presents a three-stage data-driven framework which can be applied to an operational offshore asset. The framework is applied to a case study of an operational offshore wind farm in the UK. In stage 1 of the framework a data analysis of maintenance logs and monitoring data reveals that power converter failures are most costly to the wind farm operator due to high revenue losses associated with turbine downtime. In stage 2 of the framework, artificial neural network-based failure prediction models are applied to the power converters. The models are evaluated using a novel scoring function which estimates a potential 42% reduction in maintenance costs from converter failures. Finally, in the third stage a maintenance scheduling model designed to both minimise the costs of performing maintenance and revenue losses due to maintenance downtime, is presented. This work predicts that up to 50% cost reductions compared to the baseline can be achieved by implementing the scheduling model. The data-driven techniques in this framework offer a promising route to reducing operations and maintenance costs further facilitating the deployment of offshore renewable energy assets. titulo: Predictive Vehicle Maintenance Using Simulated Industrial Conditions
titulo_norm: predictive vehicle maintenance using simulated industrial conditions
resumo: Due to the increasing trend of the automotive industry, many problems arise and the main concern is the failure of important components in vehicles, which results in reduced efficiency, increased maintenance costs, and serious breakdowns. To address this, the paper proposes a solution that decreases component failures beforehand. This new approach can advance current predictive maintenance to the next level. The system uses real-world machinery sensor data containing parameters such as air temperature, process temperature, rotational speed, torque, and tool wear to develop the models. The correlation between the parameters and their impact on the system is established. Several machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were compared to obtain performance results. The best result was achieved by the XGBoost algorithm with an accuracy of 0.989, followed by the Random Forest algorithm with an accuracy of 0.987. The system also incorporates an interactive web dashboard built with ReactJS, with the trained model exported as a.pkl file for easy integration and usage. This dashboard enables drivers and managers to monitor machine conditions and receive immediate results, where any unit showing a higher failure probability is flagged early. The proposed solution demonstrates potential for development into a large-scale IoT system and contributes to edge computing. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Dynamic Observability for Automated ML Pipelines in Predictive Maintenance for Industrial IoT
titulo_norm: dynamic observability for automated ml pipelines in predictive maintenance for industrial iot
resumo: The widespread uptake of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies has revolutionized predictive maintenance through real-time monitoring and fault prediction. Increasing complexity in automated machine learning (ML) pipelines, however, requires greater transparency, traceability and resilience. This work presents a new framework for dynamic observability of predictive maintenance pipelines for IIoT systems. The solution of choice combines modern observability features like Grafana, Prometheus, and mltrace with deep neural networks like LSTM and transformers for real-time monitoring, tracing and optimizing all pipeline elements. Employing the NASA C-MAPSS data set, the system efficiently eliminates noise and performs dynamic feature extraction using moving averages and time derivatives. The main innovations are approximation-based metric assessments, streaming data ingest through reservoir sampling and count-min sketch, and end-to-end metric consolidation through ML metrics fused with operational KPIs. The observability framework facilitates anomaly detection, diagnosis of performance degradations and recovery on auto-pilot, improving model accuracy, lessening feature staleness and pipeline latency as well as throughput. Case studies illustrate its power in the identification of data drifts, fix of feature corruption, and optimization of model output towards business objectives. Empirical findings indicate an 8.2% increase in accuracy, 11.5% precision and 25% reduction in latency in preprocessing, confirming the performance of the framework. Feature staleness and corruption scores also decreased significantly, confirming improved data integrity. Visual analyses also confirm classifier stability and feature freshness improvements. In general, the dynamic observability framework provides a scalable and adaptive platform for predictive maintenance in IIoT, enhancing operational efficiency, reliability and self-healing capabilities.  © 2025 World Scientific Publishing Company.

titulo: A Framework for Structural Monitoring: Deep Learning and Digital Twin for Anomaly Detection
titulo_norm: a framework for structural monitoring deep learning and digital twin for anomaly detection
resumo: Structural monitoring plays an important role in ensuring the safety and longevity of infrastructure; nevertheless, conventional methods frequently lack the capacity for continuous and predictive analysis. This study presents an advanced Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) system that integrates IoT, Digital Twin (DT), and Deep Learning (DL) to automate the recognition of issues with structure and enhance preventive maintenance. The methodology entails obtaining vibrational data from MEMS accelerometer sensors, analyzing it with a Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE), and visualizing the anomalies immediately within the digital twin of the monitored structure. The deep learning model, trained on temporal sequences of vibration signals acquired during normal operating conditions, acquires a concise description of standard structural behaviour. During the inference phase, the reconstruction error is a metric to detect substantial deviations and produce real-time alerts. The paper delineates the issue, current advancements, methodology employed, outcomes, and a comparison with conventional procedures. The findings underscore the potential of merging IoT, DT, and DL to enhance structural monitoring, facilitating more efficient infrastructure management and mitigating the risk of unforeseen failures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: A Hybrid ML Framework Integrating CAI and EFRI Metrics for Smart Predictive Maintenance of Power Transformers
titulo_norm: a hybrid ml framework integrating cai and efri metrics for smart predictive maintenance of power transformers
resumo: Power transformers produce rich multimodal telemetry (SCADA, DGA, FRA/EFRI, thermal imaging) that can enable predictive maintenance, but practical adoption is hindered by delayed fault detection, fragile performance when sensors are missing or asynchronous, and poorly calibrated risk outputs. The study presents Synapse-PdM, a physics-aware, causal, Bayesian multimodal Transformer that fuses modality-specific encoders with a causal disentanglement module, a hierarchical cross-modal mixture-of-experts Transformer, and a Temporal Graph Neural Network to capture topology-driven propagation. Synapse-PdM issues Bayesian survival-based EFRI curves and conformalized RUL quantiles, trained under a composite loss combining censored survival likelihood, quantile RUL losses, physics-informed regularization, causal penalties, self-supervised pretraining, and a decision-aware cost term. On held-out time-split evaluations Synapse-PdM achieves AUC-ROC 0.995, PR-AUC 0.968, RUL-MAE 4.8 days, and detects 82% of failures at least seven days ahead; Brier score is 0.060 and expected annual maintenance cost under the test cost model reduces to 9.15M. These results translate to earlier, better-calibrated alerts, fewer false alarms, and substantive operational savings, supporting pilot deployment in utility environments. The model's interpretability and uncertainty outputs enable actionable maintenance decisions and facilitate regulator acceptance and scalability.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Integration of AI and ML for Anomaly Detection in SSD Validation Logs

resumo: The explosive growth of data-intensive workloads has made solid-state drives (SSDs) a critical infrastructure building block that requires unprecedented monitoring for reliability. This work proposes SMART (SSD Monitoring and Anomaly Recognition Technology), an end-to-end AI-based system that achieves 96.7 % detection accuracy with 4.2 % false positive, far superior to prior threshold-based schemes. Our ensemble system combines gradient boosting machines, isolation forests, and deep neural networks with explainable AI features for real-time anomaly detection across heterogeneous SSD populations. Scalable validation across 5,000 production validation logs results in 35% reduced surprise failures, 28% in maintenance cost, and 23 % system availability gain. The adaptive learning and distributed design enable scalable monitoring of up to 5,000 SSDs in parallel with sub-second response time. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: UAV-Imagery Based Remote Sensing For Building Crack Detection Using Mask R-CNN
titulo_norm: uav imagery based remote sensing for building crack detection using mask r cnn
resumo: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are a common inspection tool for infrastructure since they can access distant areas and acquire high-resolution visual data at low cost and in a safe manner. Building on this capability, this paper presents an automated crack detection pipeline from aerial images captured by UAVs. The central system is an adaptation-transferred fine-tuned Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) model for building crack detection. To address the limitations of conventional models, particularly far-distance hairline crack detection from aerial images, we leverage data augmentation and UAV-specific training data to enhance robustness. Although previous state-of-the-art deep learning methods are only configured to detect cracks at distances of 3-4 meters which is not viable while performing a building inspection, our system has consistent performance upto approximately 20 meters. Experimental tests on real UAV images validate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed method for structural health monitoring and large-scale infrastructure inspection. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Predictive Modelling of Dust Accumulation in Air Conditioners using Support Vector Machines
titulo_norm: predictive modelling of dust accumulation in air conditioners using support vector machines
resumo: Recent studies have shown increasing concerns about indoor air quality and air conditioning efficiency, particularly in urban areas. Dust accumulation in air conditioning (AC) units degrades air quality while simultaneously reducing system performance and energy efficiency. This research explores a machine learning approach to detect dust inside AC systems using multi-sensor data. Real-time measurements including temperature, humidity, airflow rate, power consumption, particulate matter (PM2.5), CO2 concentration, and filter usage hours were gathered from a prototype monitoring setup. The study employed a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier to differentiate between "Normal"and "Dusty"operational states. Sensor data underwent pre-processing and normalization to enhance model performance. Results indicate strong classification accuracy from the SVM model, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying dust accumulation through sensor-driven patterns. The findings highlight SVM's potential application in predictive maintenance for AC units, ultimately contributing to energy optimization and improved indoor air quality. The SVM model achieved a classification accuracy of 91%, effectively distinguishing between dusty and normal conditions. These results validate the model's applicability in real-world environments for early dust detection and maintenance planning. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Layout-Aware Self-Correcting Prompts for Multimodal LLM Parking Lot Monitoring
titulo_norm: layout aware self correcting prompts for multimodal llm parking lot monitoring
resumo: Parking-lot monitoring is a facility-management task in which a system infers the occupancy and accessibility of predefined spaces from fixed-camera imagery. The scene typically contains many visually similar objects arranged in a stable spatial layout, which remains challenging for current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) that often misbind objects and locations. In prior work, we proposed a binding-aware, grid-based spatial prompting scheme that embeds the parking layout directly into the prompt and anchors vehicles to discrete spatial 'slots', improving slot-occupancy and obstruction detection without retraining or additional sensors. This paper extends that architecture with a layout-aware self-correcting loop around the same general-purpose MLLM. A judgment module evaluates grid-based predictions against basic layout constraints and, when violations occur, augments the prompt with explicit textual feedback and requests a single revised prediction. Experiments on real parking scenes comparing vanilla prompting, the previous grid-based method, and the extended method show that layout-aware self-correcting prompts reduce both occupancy errors and logically inconsistent configurations, while preserving low deployment cost. This provides a simple way to couple foundation models with domain-specific spatial rules in safety-relevant facility monitoring. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo_norm: artificial intelligence for predictive maintenance and energy optimization in renewables
resumo: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a pivotal technology that heralds modern progress in all fields and is capable of addressing complex issues that depend on big data in a timely and rapid manner. As for renewable energy systems in general and photovoltaic energy in particular, AI has proven to be indispensable, facilitating optimal energy management by monitoring equipment in real time and predicting future maintenance while increasing production and reducing expenses. Deep neural networks, evolutionary algorithms, and hybrid neuro-fuzzy models constitute advanced techniques that leverage AI to improve energy forecasting, optimize resource allocation, and automate control of systems more intelligently. titulo: Heat Exchanger Classifications and Their Areas of Application
titulo_norm: heat exchanger classifications and their areas of application
resumo: Heat exchangers are indispensable components in thermal management systems, enabling precise and efficient energy transfer between fluids or solids. They serve as critical enablers of energy efficiency, sustainability, and operational reliability across industries such as power generation, HVAC, chemical processing, aerospace, and waste heat recovery. This chapter presents a comprehensive analysis of heat exchanger classifications, encompassing flow arrangements, construction geometries, heat transfer mechanisms, surface compactness, number of fluids, and transfer processes. Advanced designs, including plate-fin, spiral, and extended-surface heat exchangers, effectively address industry challenges such as fouling, pressure drops, and space constraints. Innovations in materials, nanotechnology, and advanced coatings further enhance thermal and mechanical performance, ensuring robust functionality under diverse operating conditions. The chapter also outlines critical selection criteria, emphasizing their role in applications such as cryogenics, chemical synthesis, and data center cooling. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning is revolutionizing heat exchanger technology, introducing intelligent classification systems, optimized designs, and real-time monitoring capabilities. These advancements enhance heat transfer efficiency, enable predictive maintenance, and facilitate fault detection, ensuring superior performance and minimal operational downtime. This chapter underscores that by incorporating state-of-the-art designs and advanced technologies, heat exchangers are pivotal in addressing global energy and sustainability challenges. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Sunil Kumar, Kavita Rathore, and Debjyoti Banerjee; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Bibliometric analysis of innovative technology use in sustainable facilities management for smart city development
titulo_norm: bibliometric analysis of innovative technology use in sustainable facilities management for smart city development
resumo: Purpose In Africa, technological adoption in facility management (FM) is hindered by knowledge gaps, high costs and outdated infrastructure. This study aims to examine the role of innovative technology in sustainable FM (SFM) for Smart Cities through a bibliometric analysis to identify trends, themes and gaps. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus as the primary data source, covering publications from 2014 to 2024. Data was analysed using VOSviewer to visualise publication networks, keyword clusters and citation relationships. A systematic search and content analysis were applied to ensure relevant document inclusion and thematic exploration. Findings Research interest in this field has grown significantly since 2021, with the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, digital twin and building information modelling emerging as dominant technologies. China leads in publications, while Spain has the highest citation impact. However, international collaboration remains weak, particularly in Africa highlighting the need for stronger interdisciplinary research networks. titulo: AI-Driven Offshore Integrity Management: XGBoost Forecasting with Reinforcement Learning Scheduling
titulo_norm: ai driven offshore integrity management xgboost forecasting with reinforcement learning scheduling
resumo: Offshore asset integrity is constrained by harsh marine conditions, restricted accessibility, and the high cost of mobilization, with corrosion remaining a significant threat to structural reliability. To address this, a standards-based predictive maintenance framework is proposed, integrating machine learning (ML) forecasting with reinforcement learning (RL)-based scheduling. A hybrid simulation, aligned with DNV-RP-G101 guidelines for risk-based inspection, was developed to generate wall-thickness degradation data across 10 monitoring points over a 10-year period, incorporating environmental variability and maintenance resets. Four ML models: Random Forest, Linear Regression, XGBoost, and Support Vector Machine, were benchmarked for six-month-ahead predictions. XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy, with mean absolute errors generally below 0.17 mm and R2 values above 0.90, outperforming other models in capturing non-linear degradation patterns. Building on these forecasts, an RL agent optimized inspection scheduling, producing 342 decisions of which 73% were classified as Safe, 27% as Unnecessary, and none as Risky. The integrated XGBoost-RL framework therefore provides an auditable, standards-compliant workflow that links degradation monitoring to inspection scheduling. The study demonstrates that AI-driven, risk-aware approaches can significantly improve the efficiency, safety, and costeffectiveness of offshore corrosion management. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: From Legacy to Intelligent IIoT Systems: Automation, Scalability and Elasticity
titulo_norm: from legacy to intelligent iiot systems automation scalability and elasticity
resumo: The Internet of Things (IoT) revolution is reshaping how physical devices embedded with software connect to the Internet, facilitating seamless data exchange and driving automation. Industrial IoT (IIoT) extends these capabilities to industrial devices and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), driving Intelligent Manufacturing. This integration supports advanced applications like remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) optimization, enhancing production efficiency, adaptability, and decisionmaking. However, managing the vast amounts of data generated requires scalable, automated software architectures. Many small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) face challenges in building such systems due to limited resources and expertise, often starting with manual data collection and basic automation.This paper presents a solution: a fully automated, configurable, and scalable software architecture for Intelligent Manufacturing. Our system has been operational for almost one and a half years on 21 plants, processing about 17K tasks, amounting to more than three months of computations. The experimental results show that automation and elasticity have been needed by such systems since the beginning, while scalability is not required during an initial experimentation phase.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Cloud Based Task Management System for Building Inspection Using Drones and Deep Learning Techniques
titulo_norm: cloud based task management system for building inspection using drones and deep learning techniques
resumo: Building inspections are traditionally labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to human error, particularly when assessing large structures or hard-to-reach façades. Conventional methods also lack scalability and real-time defect detection capabilities. To address these challenges, this paper presents a cloud based, end-to-end unmanned aerial vehicles(UAV)-assisted building inspection framework that integrates autonomous data acquisition, cloud computing, and deep learning. High-resolution façade images are captured using UAVs and seamlessly uploaded to Amazon Web Services (AWS) S3 for cloud based storage. Images are automatically filtered for quality and analyzed using a You Only Look Once (YOLOv11) deep learning model, achieving 97% mean Average Precision (mAP) in crack detection after applying advanced data augmentation strategies. Additionally, 3D building models are reconstructed using COLMAP to provide comprehensive structural documentation. Results are delivered through an interactive Flask-based web dashboard, providing real-time visualization and structural health insights. By leveraging UAV automation, cloud scalability, and state-of-the-art deep learning, the proposed system overcomes key limitations of traditional inspection methods. It offers a more accurate, efficient, and scalable solution for structural health monitoring. © 2026 IEEE.

titulo: Integration of building information modeling and machine learning for predictive maintenance
titulo_norm: integration of building information modeling and machine learning for predictive maintenance
resumo: The integration of building information modeling (BIM) and machine learning (ML) holds significant promise in revolutionizing the field of predictive maintenance for built environments. As our world becomes increasingly urbanized, the efficient operation and maintenance of buildings and infrastructure are critical for sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and occupant safety. This research explores the convergence of BIM and ML to advance predictive maintenance strategies, enhancing the overall performance and longevity of structures. Predictive maintenance involves the proactive identification of potential equipment failures and structural issues before they lead to costly downtime or catastrophic failures. BIM is a comprehensive digital representation of a building or infrastructure asset that serves as an ideal platform for capturing, managing, and visualizing relevant data. By integrating ML algorithms into BIM systems, the potential to predict and prevent maintenance issues becomes a powerful reality. The research explores the potential benefits of the integration of BIM and ML for predictive maintenance: 1. Data integration and fusion: BIM contains a wealth of structured data about building geometry, equipment specifications, and maintenance history. By integrating this data with real-time sensor data and ML algorithms, a holistic view of asset health can be established. 2. Predictive analytics: ML models can be trained to analyze historical data patterns to predict equipment failures or structural degradation. These predictions enable timely maintenance interventions, reducing downtime and maintenance costs. 3. Risk assessment: BIM-ML integration allows for the assessment of risk factors associated with various maintenance strategies, aiding in the prioritization of critical maintenance tasks. 4. Resource optimization: ML algorithms can optimize maintenance scheduling, personnel allocation, and resource utilization, ensuring that maintenance efforts are efficient and cost-effective. 5. Resilience enhancement: By predicting and preventing maintenance issues, BIM-ML systems can enhance the resilience of structures, making them more capable of withstanding unforeseen events. The study discusses case studies and research findings from various sectors, including commercial real estate, infrastructure, and transportation. These studies demonstrate the potential impact of BIM-ML integration on predictive maintenance, highlighting its ability to transform maintenance practices from reactive to proactive. The study concludes that the integration of BIM and ML for predictive maintenance represents a pivotal advancement in the field of facility management and infrastructure development. Leveraging BIM as a foundational platform, researchers are poised to redefine maintenance strategies, making them more efficient, cost-effective, and resilient in the face of an ever-evolving urban landscape. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. titulo: Efficient Smart Water Distribution Optimization Integrating IoT and Graph Neural Networks
titulo_norm: efficient smart water distribution optimization integrating iot and graph neural networks
resumo: The effective management of Water Distribution Networks (WDNs) is essential for a sustainable municipal water supply. This study presents an intelligent water distribution optimisation system that combines Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to improve operational efficiency. The system gathers real-time sensor data, such as pressure, flow rate, and node demand, to simulate spatio-temporal dynamics and guide decision-making. A GNNbased design enables precise leakage prediction, anomaly detection, and enhanced flow routing across the network. Experiments conducted on publicly accessible WDN graph datasets reveal that the proposed methodology attains a leak detection accuracy of 95.8 % and a flow prediction Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.34 L/s, improving traditional machine learning models, including Random Forests and Support Vector Machines. The model demonstrates scalability and little inference latency, making it appropriate for extensive implementation. resumo: Effective and robust management of underground electric cable infrastructure is at the core of the smart city. Traditional fault detection and maintenance incorporate reactive approaches, causing extended outages, high operating costs, and public safety hazards. In this paper, an end-to-end AI system is presented for real-time monitoring, fault classification, and predictive maintenance of underground power cables. The architecture integrates multi-modal sensor networks, machine learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Random Forests (RF), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, and a geospatial digital twin interface to facilitate an integrated smart asset management system. Implemented in a 250 km pilot zone of a Southeast Asian smart city, the system achieved 94.6% fault detection accuracy, 40.3% decrease in mean time to repair and 37.1% less cost for maintenance tasks. titulo: Predictive Maintenance Automation: Artificial Maintenance Management Agent (AMMA) Framework
titulo_norm: predictive maintenance automation artificial maintenance management agent amma framework
resumo: This paper describes an innovative Artificial Maintenance Management Agent (AMMA) designed to detect and predict anomalies in machinery equipment, besides managing spare parts orders. The primary focus is on leveraging deep learning models and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to facilitate real-time maintenance and improve user experience respectively. This paper will show how to reduce downtimes, extend the equipment's useful life, and enhance the cost efficiency of inventory management. The approach involves the integration of state-of-the-art deep learning models for the detection and prediction of machine faults, with Large Language Models (LLMs) for interactive user engagement and inventory management. AMMA is architected to continuously learn from real-time operational data stored in a database, enabling it to identify patterns of potential failures. Additionally, it demonstrates current and future predictions on a dashboard. Through its natural language processing capabilities, the agent interacts with maintenance personnel, providing actionable insights and automating spare parts ordering for current and future failures. Preliminary results demonstrate that AMMA exceeded an accuracy of 90% in detecting anomalies in a simulated boiler fault dataset, with loss function value below 0.19, a precision higher than 0.93, a recall higher than 0.93 and a F1 score higher than 0.88 in test set. Showing a high capability to accurately detect machine anomalies before they escalate into costly failures. In addition, models that can be implemented in the agent for failure prediction have shown an accuracy score exceeding 90% in predicting the failures in a 3W dataset which is a public dataset for undesirable real events in oil wells. Observations highlight AMMA's potential to transform maintenance strategies from reactive to proactive, ultimately leading to enhanced safety. The use of the LLM OpenAI API model to enhance the user experience, besides suggesting spare parts according to the failure type, reduces operational costs and human error and increases productivity. The novelty of the proposed AMMA lies in introducing an application of deep learning and LLMs to enhance maintenance effectiveness, offering a unique solution and a step ahead of the current computerized maintenance management system (CMMS). It provides an AI-powered framework for predictive maintenance management, thereby enhancing existing solutions and advancing the state of knowledge in the industry. titulo: A Comprehensive Framework for Automated Facade Defect Evaluation Using Deep Learning
titulo_norm: a comprehensive framework for automated facade defect evaluation using deep learning
resumo: Evaluation of facade degradation is crucial to determining the need for further examination and maintenance, safeguarding the structural health of the building. Traditional evaluation methods rely on visual inspection and subjective judgment by surveyors, which requires working at heights and manual detection and severity assessment. This process is timeconsuming, poses safety risks, and may result in potential errors. To address these challenges, unmanned vehicles have been deployed for building inspection tasks, saving time and minimizing safety concerns. Additionally, diverse deep learning techniques have been utilized to automate the visual evaluation process and reduce subjective errors to classify, detect, and segment defects. However, previous research has primarily focused on improving image processing accuracy without incorporating the entire evaluation process into industry evaluation standards. In this paper, we propose a framework for automated building facade defect evaluation that can be applied to both unmanned and manned data collection systems. Our approach employs the deep neural network for defect segmentation. The trained model accurately recognizes individual defects and extracts their properties, such as width, length, and area using morphological operations. Following ISO standards, evaluation results are automatically obtained within defined effective evaluation areas. Furthermore, defect information and evaluation results are registered to a model generated with 3D reconstruction techniques, providing a valuable reference for experts in formulating maintenance plans. Finally, experiments are conducted on a tall building to verify the effectiveness of our proposed method.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Developments in Optical Fiber Network Fault Detection Methods: An Extensive Analysis
titulo_norm: developments in optical fiber network fault detection methods an extensive analysis
resumo: With the help of the continuing evolution of communication technologies, optical fiber networks have been identified to be the leading platform for today advanced data transmission systems characterized by very high bandwidth and minimal attenuation losses. However, maintaining their dependability raises a concern that forms a major problem; identifying and correcting defects likely to cause service downtime, data loss, and inefficient performances. Other conventional approaches to fault detection, such as the OTDR systems, offer basic solutions; however, their fundamental drawbacks include the issues of precision, scalability, and cost, most evident in modern large-scale networks. This paper aims at providing a detailed characterization of fault detection techniques in Optical Fiber Networks and limitation of such techniques before implementing machine learning techniques. The use of state-of-art-ML techniques such as CNNs, LSTMs, and anomaly detection models shows improved capabilities of fault prediction, fault detection, and fault classification. These approaches improve real time monitoring and control, facilitate predictive maintenance, and dispositions and resource productivity enhancing tremendously the networks availability. Through the comparison of several cases with the application of ML-based solutions for fault detection with the ordinary techniques, such as OTDR, the paper demonstrates the advantages of the proposed ML approaches to reduce the costs of network operations and to guarantee the scalability to the larger networks. These works provide the direction towards more intelligent, robust and more efficient fault ML techniques that can revolutionize the field of optical communication systems . © 2025 University of Bahrain. titulo: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance in Semiconductor SEM Equipment
titulo_norm: machine learning for predictive maintenance in semiconductor sem equipment
resumo: Predictive maintenance has emerged as a pivotal strategy in the semiconductor industry, leveraging machine learning algorithms to anticipate equipment failures and optimize maintenance schedules. Semiconductor manufacturing facilities rely on complex machinery and equipment to produce integrated circuits and other semiconductor devices. Any unexpected downtime or equipment failure can lead to significant production losses and costly repairs. Predictive maintenance stands out from other maintenance categories as it precludes any failures to equipment components. By implementing predictive maintenance solutions powered by machine learning, semiconductor companies can monitor the health of their equipment in real-time, detect potential issues before they escalate into failures, and schedule maintenance proactively to minimize downtime. In this paper, the application of predictive maintenance techniques within semiconductor manufacturing is explored, focusing on the development and deployment of machine learning models to predict equipment failures based on sensor data collected from scanning electron microscope (SEM) metrology equipment. The approach adopted in this study involves simulating sensor output data from wafer runs, training machine learning models on the generated dataset, and deploying the models as real-time inference endpoints. By integrating Azure Machine Learning Designer and Power BI, the accuracy and performance of the predictive maintenance model is assessed. Results of the study demonstrate the efficacy of machine learning in accurately forecasting equipment failures, thereby minimizing downtime and optimizing operational efficiency in semiconductor manufacturing facilities. Overall, this study underscores the transformative potential of predictive maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, paving the way for enhanced operational resilience and sustained competitiveness in the industry. © 2025 IISE Annual Conference and Expo 2025, Conference Proceedings. titulo: Physics-informed anomaly and fault detection for wind energy systems using deep CNN and adaptive elite PSO-XGBoost
titulo_norm: physics informed anomaly and fault detection for wind energy systems using deep cnn and adaptive elite pso xgboost
resumo: Wind energy systems require fault diagnosis that identifies faults despite data inconsistencies. This study addresses challenges in supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems for monitoring wind turbine conditions from imbalanced data representation and error vulnerability. It examines the efficacy of adaptive elite-particle swarm optimization (AEPSO)-tuned extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) on an imbalanced SCADA dataset for wind turbine fault classification. The methodology integrates the resampled dataset with t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding represented deep learning features. Employing AEPSO-XGBoost classifier trained on merged SCADA and deep learning data from a physics-informed deep convolutional neural network forms the basis of the fault (alarm) classification model. The AEPSO-XGBoost regressor is validated across three distinct rear bearing temperature datasets, facilitating parameter optimization and model robustness. Also, this study explores supervised and unsupervised anomaly detection models using PDCNN and AEPSO-XGBoost with rear-bearing temperature data. Findings exhibit substantial fault classification and prediction enhancements by merging resampled SCADA data with deep learning features. Moreover, results show that applying AEPSO-XGBoost can significantly improve anomaly detection metrics. Through AEPSO-XGBoost's efficacy in enhancing fault prediction within imbalanced SCADA datasets, the study proposes an integrated framework for fault classification and anomaly detection as an innovative predictive maintenance system for wind energy systems. © 2025 The Author(s). titulo: Environmental Sensor-Driven CNC Defect Identification using HS-Fuzzy and LD-TS-LSTM
titulo_norm: environmental sensor driven cnc defect identification using hs fuzzy and ld ts lstm
resumo: Higher precision is increased through efficient and accurate CNC defect detecting. They have faced complex and time-varying operating conditions in the past two decades of high-technological changes in conventional detection and these complexities have facilitated a more open door to a new and more precise real-time defect identification process. The emphasis here is on building HS-Fuzzy based LD-TS-LSTM using the inputs of environment sensors and processing them using CNC real time with a view to identifying potential errors in advance and preventing faults. We introduce a combined method of HS-Fuzzy and LD-TS-LSTM, which is built on the environmental sensor data, to detect and forecast defects in CNC machines. Findings of the suggested approach are much improved over current models, like CNN, SVM, and Random Forest, achieving a greater degree of accuracy and precision and high recall regarding defects detection, and reducing the Root Mean Error (RME) significantly. This combination methodology greatly enhances the accuracy of CNC defect detection and also has potential solutions in predictive maintenance and fault detection to improve operational efficiency and lessen downtime in the industry.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Predictive Maintenance of Induction Motor using Machine Learning Algorithms
titulo_norm: predictive maintenance of induction motor using machine learning algorithms
resumo: With the advent in industrial technologies, it is mandatory to identify the fault occurring in induction motors at early stages since prolonged defects can severely damage the motor and lead to expensive downtimes in industries. Early identification also helps in reducing the time and maintenance costs. Condition monitoring techniques prove to be a better solution surpassing the traditional methods like manual inspections and reactive maintenance by detecting unexpected breakdowns and facilitating the implementation of proactive measures. Predictive Maintenance using data-driven methods can be leveraged using Machine Learning to detect the faults in the incipient stages. This research focuses on using MATLAB machine learning approaches to identify the broken rotor bar defect that occurs in induction motors.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: IoT-Enabled Transformer Health Monitoring and Oil Level Detection
titulo_norm: iot enabled transformer health monitoring and oil level detection
resumo: Power transformers are very important in stability and reliability of electrical distribution network. Premature failures due to overloading, degradation of insulation, or loss of oil can be extremely damaging to equipment, with long-term loss, and financial losses. Conventional transformer maintenance approaches, which are periodically oriented and rely on manual diagnostics, are not always effective to ensure the lack of sudden failures and do not allow real-time monitoring. This paper introduces a temperature monitoring and fault detection system on Power transformers with IoT enabling, which will increase the operational safety, efficiency, and predictive maintenance features. The system combines several sensors, such as temperature, voltage, current, and ultrasonic level-sensors of oil, which are connected to Arduino Uno microcontroller. The ESP8266 Wi-Fi module maintains real-time data on a local LCD screen and at the same time transmits the data to a cloud-based mobile application. The system gives real-time alerts in case any of the parameters that are being monitored surpasses preset limits, and this allows prompt action to be taken to avoid disastrous failures. The ultrasonic sensor also enables one to sense the illegal oil extraction or unexpected change in oil level which tackles the issue of security. Augmentation with the smart grid infrastructure also facilitates the use of advanced energy management and predictive maintenance control techniques. Through the experimental analysis, it can be stated that the proposed system is dependable in the context of identifying abnormal operating conditions, improving the monitoring of the transformer health, and minimizing the downtime, which makes it a cost-efficient and an efficient approach to the contemporary power distribution network. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Example Study of Applications Based on YOLOv8+CNN Fusion Architecture
titulo_norm: example study of applications based on yolov8 cnn fusion architecture
resumo: The aim of this study is to deeply analyze human traffic and behavioral patterns using deep learning techniques and physical models. A behavioral pattern classification method combining YOLOv8 and convolutional neural networks is proposed for automatically detecting and estimating the number of parallel actors and total visitors. Experimental results show that the method has high accuracy in cross-scenario applications and is capable of predicting traffic patterns and visitor counts from features. In addition, the study analyzed the mechanical differences between the different travel directions of the foot traffic in the area, and the results showed that there are significant differences in the pressure and loss generated by the different travel directions on the structures at different locations in the area. The accuracy of the model was verified by predicting the service life of the structure using a physical model. This study provides a scientific basis for the optimization of public building design and facility maintenance management, which can effectively improve the use efficiency and safety of building facilities in public venues, and has good adaptability in different application scenarios. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Digital Twin Method for Lifetime Prediction of Critical Components in Drip Irrigation Tape Production Line
titulo_norm: digital twin method for lifetime prediction of critical components in drip irrigation tape production line
resumo: Drip irrigation tape production lines are fundamental to modern agriculture, where the performance and lifespan of critical components play a decisive role in ensuring production efficiency and operational reliability. Among these components, bearings serve as essential elements, yet they are particularly susceptible to wear, corrosion, and other stress-induced degradations during extended operation. Such vulnerabilities often result in unpredictable failures that disrupt the entire production line. To address this challenge, this study presents a digital twin methodology for accurately predicting the lifespan of bearings in drip irrigation tape production lines. This approach integrates real-time sensor data, simulation models, and advanced machine learning techniques to establish a dynamic, data-driven framework for predictive maintenance. Bearings, as the critical focus, are modeled both physically and through data-driven methods. High-precision sensors are deployed to monitor temperature, vibration, rotational speed, and load, providing comprehensive operational data. The raw data undergoes preprocessing to eliminate noise and anomalies, ensuring robust inputs for predictive algorithms. The study leverages attention mechanisms combined with bidirectional long short-term memory networks (Bi-LSTM) to forecast the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings under diverse operational conditions while accounting for dynamic environmental influences. The methodology employs SolidWorks software to construct a detailed bearing model, which is subsequently imported into Ansys software for simulation analysis. A dynamic digital twin model is developed by mapping real-time operational data onto the virtual simulation environment, facilitating continuous model updates. This enables highly accurate condition monitoring and lifespan prediction of bearings. Experimental validation on a real-world drip irrigation tape production line demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing predictive accuracy and real-time adaptability. The outcomes of this study include the development of a robust digital twin framework tailored to bearings in drip irrigation tape production lines, a high-precision methodology for lifespan prediction, and verification of its substantial potential in reducing maintenance costs and minimizing downtime. By advancing the predictive maintenance of bearings, this research contributes to the broader digitalization and intelligent transformation of agricultural production systems. Furthermore, the proposed methodology is scalable and adaptable, offering applicability across other agricultural and industrial domains. © 2025 ASABE. All rights reserved.

titulo: Quantum Machine Learning Applications in Ships: A Review
titulo_norm: quantum machine learning applications in ships a review
resumo: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) can transform the maritime sector by combining artificial intelligence (AI), deep machine learning and quantum computing in naval engineering and ship management. Quantum computing, when compared with classical computing, offers greater performance and cost efficiency by incorporating well-known principles from quantum physics, such as superposition and entanglement. In complex naval contexts, QML technology can enable the quick optimization of fuel-efficient routes, large-scale data processing, and enhanced forecasting models for weather and ocean conditions, which are crucial for optimal navigation and planning in dynamic marine environments. QML accelerates real-time sensor data analysis, facilitating the earlier detection of equipment failures and improving the overall operational efficiency of ships. In addition, to optimize maritime logistics challenges such as fleet management, port congestion, and cargo scheduling, QML can offer faster and more efficient solutions than classical AI and ML algorithms. In addition, quantum cryptography strengthens the communication security between ships, ship owners, and ports, while its ability to process high-dimensional noisy data more efficiently improves autonomous ship navigation and decision-making. This includes improved situational awareness and precise obstacle avoidance. Finally, QML could deliver revolutionary advantages to the shipping industry, guaranteeing more robust and secure global marine operations by facilitating more sustainable and efficient practices with reduced costs, as well as by enhancing safety through more effective predictive maintenance and advanced cybersecurity. © 2025 The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG.

titulo: The Evolution of AI in Product Development
titulo_norm: the evolution of ai in product development
resumo: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly altered the process of product development, revolutionizing the way things are conceived, improved and introduced to the market. This chapter offers an analysis of the progression of AI in product creation, starting from its initial stages with rule-based systems to the current advanced machine learning algorithms and AI-driven processes. This chapter commences with a historical synopsis, documenting the earliest incorporation of AI into product development using fundamental computational approaches. Subsequently, it delves into the revolutionary influence of machine learning, which has facilitated the use of data-driven methods for design and optimization. The current trends in AI-driven product development are emphasized, demonstrating technologies such as generative design, natural language processing and AI-driven simulations. These technologies improve the processes of generating ideas, creating prototypes and manufacturing. In addition, the chapter explores the utilization of artificial intelligence in the fields of smart manufacturing, quality control and predictive maintenance. The chapter examines potential future advancements, such as the integration of artificial intelligence with augmented reality to improve collaboration and the development of products that are autonomous. It offers a thorough examination of the historical progression, present state and future prospects of AI in product creation, with a particular focus on its capacity to enhance product quality and efficiency. © 2026 Kanchan Naithani, Shrikant Tiwari and Shabnam Kumari.

titulo: Digital twin for smart wireless sensor networks
titulo_norm: digital twin for smart wireless sensor networks
resumo: Digital twins (DTs) are new, dynamic virtual reality replicas that mimic physical reality moments- transforming many industries along the way. This chapter explores what DTs concept, practical applications, challenges, and what may lie ahead especially when applied in the smart wireless sensor networks (WSNs) landscape. To enable simple supervision, prediction, and enhancement of compound systems, computerized replicas need to helplessly watch each other during real-time integration with the World Wide Web, artificial intelligence, device learning, machine learning, and progressive statistics analysis. There is a detailed definition of DTs in WSNs in this chapter. It includes the primary components like physical and virtual sensors, communication infrastructure, data analytics, and user interfaces as well as other important aspects like data integration and management, which are crucial since they stress how efficient strategies would be implemented to handle heterogeneous data obtained from different sensor nodes. In addition, the chapter discusses how using DTs could improve predictive maintenance strategies by anticipating and then lowering downtimes; in effect, leading to lower maintenance expenditures. The chapter also discusses how important DTs have been in evolving Internet of Things and Industry 4.0, noting that they play important roles in automating processes through optimization and facilitating digital transformation in various industries. Moreover, upon increasing network sizes, concerns on how to scale DT solutions are addressed here while considering potential alternatives that may ensure scalability and the ability to support large-scale deployments as well. In conclusion, the chapter does not fully discuss DTs’ transformative nature but also goes a step further to give a comprehensive guideline on how they are incorporated into smart WSNs and other new technologies. A foundation has been laid down for upcoming research and advancement which seeks to solve the problems we have today as well as create room for new sources of innovation and productivity gains in many areas. © 2025 Elsevier Inc. titulo: Weather-aware deep learning framework for sustainable urban surveillance and infrastructure resilience
titulo_norm: weather aware deep learning framework for sustainable urban surveillance and infrastructure resilience
resumo: Extreme weather conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and sandstorms reduce visibility, hindering reliable monitoring of urban spaces and critical infrastructure. This limitation affects structural health inspections, facility management, and public safety, key components of sustainable urban development. This study introduces a weather-aware computer vision framework designed to maintain high detection accuracy under adverse meteorological conditions, supporting resilient and climate-adaptive urban monitoring. The system employs a modular two-stage deep learning pipeline, integrating weather-specific enhancement modules (AOD-Net for dehazing, DerainNet for deraining) into a learnable adaptive fusion network. Enhanced images are processed with Faster R-CNN for high-precision object detection. Evaluations on benchmark datasets (DAWN, MS COCO, EXDARK, PASCAL VOC) demonstrate superior performance over SSD, YOLOv3, and RetinaNet, achieving mAP@ [.5:.95] of 68.93 with F1-score 0.76, recall 0.73, precision 0.79, and IoU 0.64. Image quality metrics (SSIM=0.89, PSNR=27.93 dB, MSE=101.37) confirm significant restoration capability. By ensuring accurate detection in challenging climates, the framework enables early hazard identification, improved asset management, and safer public spaces. Its scalability makes it suitable for smart city surveillance, autonomous inspection of building facades, and infrastructure resilience assessments. Future research will focus on lightweight deployment for real-time inference on edge devices, enabling cost-effective, energy-efficient, and sustainable monitoring solutions for weather-vulnerable urban environments. © 2025 International Journal of Sustainable Building Technology and Urban Development.

titulo: Unleashing AI at the Edge: Transforming Computing
titulo_norm: unleashing ai at the edge transforming computing
resumo: The convergence of edge computing with Artificial Intelligence (AI) constitutes a watershed point in technological growth, with transformational implications for a wide range of sectors. This chapter explores the mutually beneficial interaction between edge computing and AI, as well as the inherent difficulties and broad implications for the direction of computing in the future. With its decentralized processing model, edge computing puts data analysis closer to the point of origin, facilitating improved efficiency and real-time insights. Edge devices enable sophisticated cognitive processes and autonomous decision-making through seamless integration with AI algorithms. However, this integration creates architectural challenges that call for creative solutions to handle privacy and security issues and strike a balance between processing power and other resources. The chapter examines how edge computing-enabled AI can revolutionize manufacturing, transportation, healthcare, and smart cities. It shows how AI can change predictive maintenance, individualized healthcare monitoring, and urban infrastructure optimization. New advances offer avenues for collaborative applications and decentralized AI training. Federated learning models, the spread of edge AI chips and algorithms, and the democratization of AI capabilities are some of these themes. In summary, this chapter provides direction on navigating the rapidly evolving area of artificial intelligence (AI) facilitated by edge computing, encouraging collaboration and innovation to fully achieve AI's transformative potential and address digital age concerns. © 2025 Bentham Science Publishers.
